Title: PNB unit eyes up to RM600mil recurring annual income from Merdeka 118
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: PNB Merdeka Ventures Sdn Bhd expects recurring income from the completed Merdeka 118 development to reach RM500 million-RM600 million a year over the medium term.
About 70 per cent of the project's office space is already sub-leased, according to MARC Ratings.
The firm said the office component is fully leased to parent Permodalan Nasional Bhd (PNB) under a triple-net master lease.
This shields PNB Merdeka from occupancy and most property-related cost risks.
MARC said about 70 per cent of the tower's 1.6 million sq ft net lettable area (NLA) has been sub-leased.
This comprises 40 per cent, or 33 floors, sub-leased to Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank), 20 per cent to PNB and about 10 per cent to other tenants.
Occupancy is expected to rise to about 90 per cent over the next five years, with the office tower projected to generate annual net property income of about RM137 million.
MARC has affirmed its AAAIS rating on PNB Merdeka's RM6 billion Merdeka sukuk Wakalah with a stable outlook.
The rating aligns with PNB's AAA/Stable corporate credit rating, supported by PNB's unconditional and irrevocable rolling guarantee covering any shortfall in principal and profit payments under the sukuk.
MARC said for the seven-storey retail mall, which is expected to open next month, lease agreements covering 81 per cent of its 750,324 sq ft NLA have either been signed or are under negotiation, at an indicative average rental of RM11.92 per sq ft.
The Merdeka 118 development, near Stadium Merdeka and Stadium Negara, has incurred RM10.6 billion in development costs to date.
The cost was largely funded by two earlier sukuk programmes that have since been restructured into the current rated issuance.
The planned residential components are expected to add another RM1.4 billion in development costs, to be funded through a mix of borrowings and equity injections.
Two residential towers, with a combined estimated gross development value (GDV) of RM2 billion, are targeted for launch in the first half of 2027, while a serviced apartment project has an estimated GDV of RM745 million.
MARC said these residential and serviced apartment components remain exposed to demand risk amid competing developments in Kuala Lumpur.
PNB Merdeka is wholly owned by PNB and was established to undertake the Merdeka 118 project.
This includes the 118-storey Menara Merdeka Maybank, a 17-floor luxury hotel, a three-floor observation deck and the upcoming retail mall.
PNB Merdeka is also the landowner and custodian of Stadium Merdeka and Stadium Negara, both designated National Heritage sites.

Title: Indonesia warned to keep its guard against wildfire despite drop in hotspots
Article:
JAKARTA: The Indonesian government must keep its guard up against wildfires despite a recent decline in the number of hotspots, with peatland fires still prone to flare up amid persistently hot and dry weather, environmental groups said on Monday.
The Southeast Asian country has been battling its most intense wildfires in 11 years, with "super El Nino" weather driving up temperatures.
Fire and haze have also caused a spike in the number of respiratory illnesses in Indonesia and shrouded neighbouring Malaysia and Singapore in hazardous smog.
Though Indonesia's Forestry Ministry said the number of hotspots had nearly halved from Friday to Saturday, there was still high potential for peatland fires, said Putra Saptian, a campaigner with the peatland protection group Pantau Gambut.
"A reduction in hotspots should not be cited by the government as a key indicator of success, given that the characteristics of peatland fires differ from those of fires on mineral soil," he told a press conference.
"The nature of (peatland) fires, which spread through underground organic material, can trigger persistent smouldering and create the potential for fires to re-emerge," he said.
The group warned that out of 24 million hectares of Indonesia's peatland, 16 million hectares have been made more fire-prone as a result of ecosystem damage, including extensive deforestation and the depletion of water tables.
A study conducted by Pantau Gambut showed that only 3% of the peatland damaged by fires over the 2015-2019 period has been restored into forest, and the group urged the government to do more to tackle peatland degradation.
President Prabowo Subianto launched a new peatland and mangrove restoration agency last month.
The Forestry Ministry said in a statement on Sunday that it remained on high alert and would maintain efforts to contain fires, especially peat fires.
In South Sumatra, thick haze from peat fires was turning the sky yellow, with air pollution at "a very terrifying" level, said Kartika Lestari, an environmental campaigner based in  the provincial capital of Palembang.
"Dust is clinging to our clothes: imagine what that would do to our lungs," Kartika told the Monday briefing.
The air pollution index in Palembang exceeded 1,000 on Monday. A reading of above 300 is categorised as "hazardous."
At the same briefing, environment group Greenpeace called on the government to go after companies linked to the fires, including Malaysia-based firms running businesses in Indonesia.
Malaysia's Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Arthur Joseph Kurup warned at a separate briefing on Monday that "the worst is yet to come", with hot and dry conditions set to persist into the new year.

Title: ParkIt says RM5 'fee' collection at MRT facility not by its employees
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: ParkIt Malaysia has denied any involvement in the collection of a RM5 "parking fee" by an unidentified person at the Maluri Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) Park and Ride facility here.
The parking management company's denial follows complaints that went viral on social media, with MRT users expressing dissatisfaction over an individual allegedly openly collecting payment from motorists at the facility.
In a statement, ParkIt said the person collecting payment at the entrance was neither its employee nor representative.
"ParkIt does not collect any parking fees at Maluri MRT at present and does not authorise any party to collect payments on our behalf," it said.
Earlier, Threads user hnnalily uploaded a photograph of a man wearing a black collared shirt and holding up a QR code on his mobile phone, allegedly to collect parking payments online.
The user questioned the man's identity and expressed frustration over the RM5 fee.
ParkIt said it had taken action over the incident, including lodging a police report and handing over video footage of the incident to the authorities.
It also referred the incident to MRT Corp, Rapid KL, police and Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL).
Rapid KL representatives, accompanied by Prasarana auxiliary police personnel, had visited the location to inspect the area and monitor security.
"Users are advised to record the time and location of any such incident, and report it to the police via the 999 emergency line or send a direct message (DM) to ParkIt," it said.

Title: Cognitive warfare aims to blur line between truth and falsehood, says Khaled
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Cognitive warfare is no longer simply about spreading fake news, but about undermining people's ability to distinguish between what is true and false, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said.
He said malicious actors could use fabricated content, false authorities, fake news platforms and manipulated social media engagement to create an entire ecosystem of deception.
"This year, we build upon those foundations by examining how technology compresses the time available to understand events and respond.
"Firstly, the objective of cognitive threats is no longer to simply spread fake news. Instead, their aim is to undermine our ability to distinguish what is true and what is false," he said in his opening remarks at Siber Siaga 2026.
Khaled said the growing use of digital technologies and artificial intelligence had further enabled adversaries to tailor information and deception to specific groups and individuals, particularly those more susceptible to manipulation.
He said such threats were also difficult to trace as they could originate from domestic or foreign sources and involve state or non-state actors, including small groups or individuals operating far beyond Malaysia's borders.
Khaled said these developments demonstrated how closely cyber capabilities and cognitive resilience were interconnected.
"We must therefore protect not only the systems supporting our decisions, but also the integrity of the information upon which those decisions are based," he said.
He said cyber threats had grown more complex and serious, with attacks capable of disrupting critical infrastructure, stealing sensitive information and amplifying cognitive warfare.
Khaled said cyberattacks could target critical infrastructure including airports, seaports, power grids, transportation networks, banking systems, healthcare facilities and internet connectivity.
"When these systems fail, what begins as an invisible attack can quickly escalate into a national crisis," he said.
He said cyberattacks could also be used for espionage and to steal sensitive information, including personal data, national secrets, military capabilities and strategic interests.
Citing a cyberattack targeting three major United Kingdom airports in August that exposed the personal data of 8.7 million passengers, Khaled said it demonstrated the far-reaching consequences of cyberattacks even without physical disruption.
On the growing role of technology in warfare, he said machines could now process information in milliseconds, compressing the time available to understand events and respond.
"Military decisions carry consequences for sovereignty, regional stability and human lives. The speed at which a recommendation is produced cannot, by itself, determine the confidence we place in it," he said.
Khaled said commanders and operators must understand the capabilities and limitations of systems, while human responsibility and accountability must remain clear throughout the chain of command.
"No matter how advanced our systems become, the responsibility for explaining and justifying a decision must remain with the people who make it," he said.
He said Malaysia must also strengthen testing, assurance and resilience to ensure missions could continue when technology was disrupted or degraded.
"Ultimately, a cyber incident can do more than disrupt a system. It can affect what a commander knows, the options available to them, and the decisions they make," he said.
Khaled said Malaysia's resilience must therefore extend beyond preventing cyberattacks to include its ability to withstand disruption, recover quickly and sustain operations.
He also said greater investment in people was needed, as effective use of technology required personnel with technical competence, operational understanding and strong ethical conviction.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Finnish town braces for change from Google data centres
Article:
IN the northern Finnish town of Muhos, 36-year-old farmer Joni Pitkanen is preparing for life with a new neighbour – just kilometres away, tech giant Google is planning to build new data centres.
The planned data centres are part of an announced 13-billion-euro (US$15-billion) investment in Finland over the next two years – the US tech giant's single biggest investment in Europe.
A few kilometers down the gravel road that passes by Pitkanen's farm, the forest has already been cut down on land acquired by Google, with excavators now clearing the ground and rumbling trucks shuttling back and forth to the construction area located next to major power lines.
"The project is so massive that it's basically hard to really grasp, even though we're right here on the sidelines," Pitkanen said, as a few cows dozed in a meadow in front of the barn.
Google's expansion plans include the Finnish municipalities of Kajaani, Muhos and Vaala as well as Hamina, where it already operates a data centre.
The massive investment prompted US President Donald Trump to urge Google to rethink its plans in a message on his Truth Social network.
Pitkanen said he was so far "fairly positive" about the project, as it will bring "large-scale business activity" and "life" to the rural municipality with a population of only around 8,800 people.
"But of course we are concerned about... how we can prepare for the energy consumption," he added.
In his office in the small village centre, Muhos mayor Kimmo Hinno told AFP that Google's "massive investment" kept him busy these days as "no industry of this type" existed here at present.
"This will completely change the situation for the entire municipality and the Oulu region," he said, adding that he expected "thousands of workers" of different nationalities during the construction period – who will need both housing and other services.
Outside a grocery store, 60-year-old nurse Aila Heilima said she hoped the investment would "motivate young people to stay" in Muhos for work, instead of moving to bigger towns in search of job opportunities.
But Google's plans have already sparked controversy.
The Finnish Supervisory Agency (LVV) is currently investigating whether company Tuike Finland, which represents Google, had cleared more than 300 hectares of forest in Muhos without a mandatory environmental impact assessment.
[[nid:1548373]]
"In our view, operations at this construction site should be suspended until it is clarified whether the project is in compliance with the law," Hanna Halmeenpaa, chair of the board of the Finnish Association for Nature Conservation, who filed the request with the agency, told AFP at the edge of the deforested area.
"From the satellite images, we've seen that nature sites which should be preserved have also been logged," she added, explaining that the size of the clear-cut area was comparable to 420 football fields.
Google, meanwhile, told AFP in an email that "tree felling activities have been taking place in compliance with Forestry Act requirements" and they "were awaiting further guidance from LVV on this matter."
"We have conducted extensive nature surveys covering the entire area as part of the zoning and Environmental Impact Assessment processes, to ensure high-value nature zones within the sites have been protected during forestry works," said Sondre Ronander, communications manager for Google in Finland.
Finland has seen a spike in data centre investments, with its cool climate and relatively stable and cheap electricity that is mostly produced without fossil fuels thanks to nuclear plants as well as extensive wind and hydro power.
Prime Minister Petteri Orpo's right-wing government has prioritised attracting data centre investments to the Nordic country, which is grappling with record-high unemployment and sluggish economic growth.
But, as dozens of the energy guzzling centres are now under construction and many more planned by companies including Microsoft and TikTok, uncertainty around energy prices, grid capacity and environmental effects have sparked a public debate in Finland.
A citizen's initiative demanding stricter regulation regarding data centre energy use and consequences for the environment gathered more than 50,000 signatures in just three days after it opened, meaning it will have to be reviewed by parliament.
* The writer is from AFP

Title: Government looking into caning mule account holders
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:The government is reviewing and considering a proposal to impose caning as an additional punishment for specific offences involving the misuse of mule accounts.
Deputy Home Minister Datuk Seri Dr Shamsul Anuar Nasarah said the proposal was put forward to address the threat posed by financial fraud syndicates, which have become increasingly complex.
"The ministry acknowledges the situation and is prepared to review the suitability of existing penalties, as well as conduct further analysis regarding their effectiveness, appropriateness, and implications within the nation's criminal legal framework.
"Given the increasingly challenging circumstances, this review will be carried out comprehensively through engagement and coordination with stakeholders, including the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) and relevant ministries and agencies," he said.
He was replying to a question regarding the Triumph FX investment fraud case raised by Khoo Poay Tiong (PH-Kota Melaka) during the Special Chamber session at the Dewan Rakyat today.
Meanwhile, Shamsul Anuar revealed that the police had conducted 100,230 raids on fraud syndicate call centres between 2023 and August, resulting in the arrest of 9,159 individuals across the entire chain of syndicates.
He said of the total, action was taken against 36 masterminds, 74 managers, 165 supervisors, 118 individuals acting as financial managers or mule account operators, 132 information technology (IT) programmers, and 8,409 lower-level operators.
"In January to August this year alone, 3,395 raids were carried out, resulting in 3,128 arrests.
"These statistics demonstrate that police continue to intensify enforcement actions to cripple the entire operational chain of these fraud syndicates," he said.
Shamsul Anuar said this approach is crucial to ensure that enforcement actions do not merely focus on low-level perpetrators but also target those who control, manage, and profit from the criminal activities.

Title: Lawmaker says foreign doctors could help ease Sabah, Sarawak shortage
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government should consider recruiting foreign doctors to address shortages of medical officers in Sabah and Sarawak, said Bandar Kuching member of parliament Dr Kelvin Yii.
The rate of medical officers who failed to report for permanent appointments had risen from 2 per cent in 2022 to 20 per cent in 2023, around 40 per cent in 2025 and 66 per cent for hospital postings in Sabah this month, he said.
"As a short-term measure, is the government prepared to recruit foreign doctors, starting with international graduates whom we have trained ourselves at our medical universities, with appropriate patient safety safeguards?
"This should only serve as a temporary bridge, not a substitute to improve the pay and career prospects of our own doctors.
"The Malaysian Medical Association has reported rates of between 70 and 76 per cent in Sabah and Sarawak. This is no longer a warning sign. This is an emergency," Dr Yii said while debating the Health Select Committee's report in the Dewan Rakyat.
Several hospitals were struggling with severe manpower shortages, including Beluran Hospital, which received no new doctors and now has only six doctors, he said.
He said Kudat Hospital received four of 17 doctors, while Sri Aman Hospital received six of 20.
Among other measures, Dr Yii urged the government to restore percentage-based Borneo Incentive (BIW) payments for healthcare workers in Sabah and Sarawak and provide relocation assistance upfront based on actual costs.
Dr Yii also proposed establishing a Health Services Commission with the authority to determine remuneration without being bound by schemes governing the wider public service.
"Promote doctors immediately upon permanent appointment, make service in Sabah and Sarawak an incentive towards securing specialist training places.
"Clearly set the duration of mandatory service, whether 12 to 24 months, together with a commensurate package and clear career benefits afterwards," he said.
On Oct 1, the Malaysian Medical Association called on the government to restore percentage-based BIW payments to attract and retain doctors in Sabah and Sarawak.
This followed reports that up to 76 per cent of medical officers failed to report for permanent postings.

Title: Takiyuddin questions RM193.71mil court bail funds held in private account
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government should explain the status of RM193.71 million in court bail funds held in a private company's bank account instead of being transferred to the Consolidated Trust Account, Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan (PN-Kota Baru) said.
He said the funds remained in the bank account of e-Jamin operator Dapat Vista (M) Sdn Bhd as at Dec 31, 2020.
"This is not a small amount. The question is, why has this still not been resolved after five years?
"Who was responsible for ensuring that the money was transferred, and what is its current status?" he told the Dewan Rakyat today.
Takiyuddin was debating the Public Accounts Committee's (PAC) report on the management of court bail money through the e-Jamin system under the Office of the Chief Registrar of the Federal Court.
He also questioned how the company had been allowed to handle court bail transactions for five years without a formal contract with the government.
The e-Jamin system began operating in January 2020, but no formal agreement had been signed between the government and the company as of the audit in July last year.
"How could a company manage public money transactions for five years without a contract?" he asked.
Takiyuddin said the matter was particularly concerning as bail deposits were paid directly into a commercial bank account belonging to the company rather than a government or joint account.
"This is not about whether the money has gone missing. This is about the custody of public money.
"In the public sector, the most basic principle is that government money must remain under government control," he said.
He also questioned the RM4 million to RM5 million in annual interest allegedly earned from the deposits and highlighted an RM557,258 discrepancy between the e-Jamin system's records and the company's bank statement.
Takiyuddin sought clarification on how the vendor was appointed, whether the procurement was conducted through an open tender and whether the Finance Ministry had formally approved the arrangement.
He acknowledged that e-Jamin had significantly improved the bail process, reducing the time required from between four and five hours to about 15 to 30 minutes.
However, he said efficiency should not come at the expense of sound financial governance.
"This is not a question of whether the vendor is good or bad, nor whether the e-Jamin system is beneficial.
"The issue is the principle of the country's financial governance. In managing public money, efficiency must go hand in hand with accountability," he said.
He also questioned what would happen to bail money that was not subsequently claimed by guarantors or accused persons, including whether it would be classified as unclaimed money and transferred to the Treasury.
"Every sen of the people's money must be protected through a control system that is transparent, legally sound and auditable," he said.

Title: NRES: No more exemptions for companies which fail to meet emission standards
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Companies that fail to take concrete steps to reduce emissions will no longer be granted exemptions under the Environmental Quality (Clean Air) Regulations.
Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said all companies must comply with emission standards by 2030.
He said the regulations, which came into force in 2014, prohibit plants and factories from emitting more than 600 milligrammes per cubic metre.
"I issued a statement early last month that I will not be issuing any more exemptions. However, I know that the industries need time to implement the technology.
"They need to do their feasibility studies, and they need to do some renovations, some changes to implement the technology.
"For most, their exemptions will expire by January next year," he told reporters at a press conference after chairing the Concorde Club talk with senior editors at Wisma Bernama here.
Arthur said exemptions would only be granted to companies that had demonstrated steps towards implementing the necessary technology for cleaner emissions.
He said companies seeking exemptions would have to show they had started implementing the technology or taken steps towards complying with the Clean Air Regulations.
"If we are to meet our target of net zero emissions by 2050, we need to have all this in place, and we definitely need cooperation from the industries.
"I will only be granting exemptions to those that have shown steps to implement the technology. Everyone has to be fully compliant by 2030," he added.
Meanwhile, Arthur said the government would not implement the carbon tax this year as it focuses on establishing the necessary framework and policies.
He said the carbon tax was initially limited to selected industries, namely energy, steel and cement.
"However, because of rising geopolitical tensions and volatile energy prices, we wanted to give the industries some buffer, which is why we delayed the carbon tax," he said.
Arthur said the delay would also allow the government to put the proper framework in place, following the launch of the National Carbon Market Policy.
He said the government hoped to table the Climate Change Act soon, which would establish the framework, policies, regulations and enforcement powers needed to regulate emissions.
"Once that is up, then we will have the framework and the policies all clearly in place, including regulatory powers to set the emission ceiling.
"Only then will the carbon tax come into place as a penalty to polluters. As such, we're not looking for the carbon tax to be implemented this year."

Title: Saudi-led coalition says joined Yemen govt offensive against Houthis
Article:
RIYADH: The Saudi-led military coalition announced on Monday its participation in the new Yemen government offensive targeting the Iran-backed Houthis, with 100 warplanes used in dawn strikes to provide air cover for ground forces.
"100 fighter jets participated at dawn today in Operation 'Dawn of Yemen'," coalition spokesman Major General Turki al-Maliki wrote on X, using the name for the new offensive announced on Sunday.
"Round-the-clock air support for the Yemeni armed forces on the ground."
The coalition's announcement came after the Yemeni military said it launched a broad set of strikes against Houthi targets on Monday, after the country's internationally recognised government declared a new campaign to retake all territory.
The Iran-backed Houthis have made fresh gains in recent weeks, capturing swathes of the country's Red Sea coastline and territory around the Bab al-Mandab Strait – a key chokepoint for international shipping.
At war against the government, the Houthis launched a lightning offensive in September that has killed hundreds of combatants on both sides and, according to UN figures, forced more than 145,000 people to flee their homes.
Yemen is one of the poorest countries in the world and remains gripped by a vast humanitarian crisis that has unspooled since the civil war broke out in 2014.

Title: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor takes police to court over Epstein files arrest
Article:
LONDON: King Charles' younger brother, Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, is taking the police to court to challenge his arrest in February on suspicion of misconduct in public office over allegations he sent confidential government documents to Jeffrey Epstein.
Britain's Judicial Office, part of the non-political civil service which supports the courts, said on Monday a hearing would take place on Thursday after the former prince sought to quash the search warrants that were issued as part of the arrest.
Thames Valley Police, which carried out the arrest, confirmed it was engaged in legal proceedings and declined further comment.
Mountbatten-Windsor was arrested in February on suspicion of leaking government documents to Epstein when Mountbatten-Windsor was a special representative for trade between 2001 and 2011.
The second son of the late Queen Elizabeth has denied any wrongdoing in relation to Epstein, and said he regrets their friendship. His lawyer did not respond to a request for comment.
Mountbatten-Windsor was questioned all day by detectives and a Reuters photograph which captured the former prince as he left the police station showed him looking in a state of shock.
He was forced to quit all official royal duties in 2019 over his ties with disgraced financier and convicted sex offender Epstein, and was then stripped by his older brother of his titles and honours last October after further revelations about their relationship. Epstein was found dead in his Manhattan jail cell in August 2019 in what was ruled a suicide.
The judicial office said the hearing on Thursday regarded an effort by the police to restrict access to court documents. The hearing will begin in private.
News of the legal challenge was first reported by the Daily Telegraph.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fix Sabah, Sarawak doctor shortage with better incentives, parliamentary committee tells MOH
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Parliamentary Special Select Committee on Health wants the Health Ministry to review existing allowances and incentives to encourage medical officers to serve in Sabah and Sarawak.
Special Select Committee on Health member Young Syefura Othman said the refusal of medical officers to take up postings in the two states was a serious concern, with some hospitals operating with as few as three medical officers.
"I would also like to touch on the concerns in Sabah and Sarawak, where medical officers who are supposed to report for duty at several clinics and hospitals have failed to do so.
"In other words, they are not interested in serving in Sabah or Sarawak.
"Allowances and incentives remain one of the factors contributing to this situation.
"Therefore, committee members want the ministry to review the existing schemes and consider fair and meaningful incentives," she said.
Syefura was speaking when winding up the debate on the Health Select Committee's report in the Dewan Rakyat today.
She said the network of hospitals, health clinics, dental clinics and mobile services also needed to be planned to ensure treatment was provided at the appropriate level and as close to the people as possible.
Digitalisation, she said, should not simply involve replacing manual processes.
Instead, it should lead to more efficient workflows, better access to information and more effective use of healthcare workers' time, supported by adequate information and communications technology infrastructure.

Title: e-Jamin: Why is the bail system under scrutiny?
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Public Accounts Committee (PAC) found that the e-Jamin system had operated for five years without a formal government contract and raised concerns about the handling of bail deposits, including funds held in the operator's commercial accounts.
What is e-Jamin?
The e-Jamin system is an electronic court bail payment service that allows a surety, or bailor, to pay bail online on behalf of an accused person.
The system was introduced in January 2020 as part of efforts to digitise court processes and make the bail process faster and more convenient.
How does e-Jamin work?
Under the conventional bail process, a surety may have to arrange payment through a bank before the accused can be released on bail.
With e-Jamin, the surety can make the required payment online through internet banking.
The government's MyGovernment portal says the service is intended to allow an accused person to be released from custody faster and more easily. Payments are made through FPX internet banking.
Why was e-Jamin introduced?
The system was designed primarily to reduce delays in securing an accused person's release.
e-Jamin allows bail to be paid without the bailor having to physically go to a bank to obtain the necessary bail bond.
This is particularly useful when banks are closed, including when court proceedings take place outside normal banking hours.
Does e-Jamin mean the accused is automatically released?
No. e-Jamin is a payment and bail-management mechanism. It does not determine whether an accused person is entitled to bail.
The decision to grant bail, the amount involved and the conditions imposed remain matters for the court.
The bailor also remains responsible for ensuring the accused complies with the conditions of bail and attends court when required.
Why is e-Jamin now under scrutiny?
The PAC's latest report concerns how the system and bail money were administered, rather than the basic concept of making bail payments online.
e-Jamin had operated across 192 courts nationwide since Jan 10, 2020, without a formal contractual agreement with the Federal Government.
The committee also found that bail payments were held in the commercial accounts of the system's operator rather than the government's Consolidated Trust Account.
As at Dec 31, 2024, RM193.71 million in bail deposits was held in the e-Jamin account, with RM130.8 million having been invested under the operator's name, generating between RM4 million and RM5 million in annual interest, according to the PAC.
The PAC also raised concerns over the absence of a trustee arrangement, performance bond and insurance, as well as an unreconciled RM557,258 difference between system records and the operator's bank statements.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: IGP: Intelligence gathering, surveillance part of TCO duties
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Travel Control Officers (TCO) are tasked with intelligence-related duties, including establishing contact with certain parties and conducting surveillance, Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said.
Khalid, responding to questions about the role of TCOs following an incident involving Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain, said the officers came under the Special Branch.
He said intelligence gathering could involve officers establishing contact with certain parties, conducting surveillance and carrying out other operational duties.
"Such activities are normal aspects of their work and should not be misinterpreted before investigators have established the full circumstances of the incident," he said after launching the Negotiators Guidelines Book at Bukit Aman today.
Asked whether there had been a breach of standard operating procedures (SOPs) during the incident, Khalid said he could not confirm this at present.
"Normally, it would not constitute a breach of SOP, but there may be matters involving the TCO's duties within the KLIA building and the respective jurisdictions that require further investigation.
"I cannot provide further details at this stage. Let the investigation be completed," he said.
Last week, the Public Service Department said it was
awaiting the outcome
of the police investigation before deciding on the next course of action.
Its director-general Tan Sri Dr Wan Ahmad Dahlan Abdul Aziz said the department had yet to receive any report against the director-general over his actions in the viral clip showing him berating two men.
It was reported that a clip had gone viral showing a man believed to be Shuhaily berating two men, with one appearing to have been grabbed forcefully by the ears.
Besides the video,
a copy of a police report
allegedly lodged by the man who was purportedly subjected to rough treatment by Shuhaily also went viral.
Shuhaily said at a press conference that he was prepared to be investigated over the incident.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: IGP: No confirmation yet of SOP breach in KLIA altercation video
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police are uncertain if any procedural breaches took place during the viral altercation involving Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain and Travel Control Officers (TCO) at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA).
Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail, explaining the role of the Special Branch's TCOs, said they carry out intelligence-related duties, including establishing contact with certain parties and surveillance.
"Such activities are normal aspects of their work and should not be misinterpreted before investigators had established the full circumstances of the incident," he said.
Asked if there were any standard operating procedure (SOP) breaches, Khalid said he could not confirm this at present.
"Normally, it would not constitute a breach of SOP, but there may be matters involving the TCO's duties within the KLIA building and the respective jurisdictions that require further investigation.
"I cannot provide further details at this stage. Let the investigation be completed," he said.
He was speaking to reporters after launching the Negotiators Guidelines Book at Bukit Aman.
Last week, a video clip showing a man believed to be Shuhaily berating two men went viral.
The clip showed one of the men being grabbed forcefully by the ears.
Apart from the video, a copy of the supposed police report lodged by one of the two men also made its rounds on social media.
Shuhaily, at a press conference last week, said the
incident
happened during an enforcement operation targeting foreign touts at KLIA's Terminal 1.
Shuhaily and his team have also lodged a police report over what they believe may have been an attempt to tarnish his image and MCBA's.
He expressed his
readiness to be investigated
over the incident.
The Public Service Department last week said it was
awaiting the outcome of the police investigation before decidin
g on the next course of action.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zetrix AI in discussions to resolve issues as JPJ services temporarily suspended
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Zetrix AI Bhd said it is currently in discussions to resolve issues with the Road Transport Department (JPJ) following the temporary suspension of its services to the department effective today.
The company confirmed in a stock exchange filing today that JPJ services would be temporarily suspended effective Oct 5, 2026. On Oct 2, JPJ announced that services provided by MyEG Sdn Bhd and Zetrix AI Bhd under the MYEG Group as its collection agents would be suspended from 12.01 am on Oct 5.
Zetrix AI said it would make further announcements on any material development.
The clarification was issued in reference to a news article appearing in The Edge Malaysia and a notice from JPJ, both dated Oct 2, 2026, it added.
JPJ director-general Datuk Aedy Fadly Ramli said the decision to suspend the company's services was made after considering compliance with the terms and conditions of their agreements and obligations that remained unfulfilled or unresolved.
He said all JPJ services previously offered through MYEG Group channels would be suspended, while the department's services would continue as usual through official and alternative channels.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: India court seeks explanations from election body in voter list row
Article:
NEW DELHI: India's Supreme Court ordered the government and the national election body on Monday to explain decisions linked to a large-scale revision of voter rolls that prompted accusations of wrongdoing.
Opposition parties and activists have organised protests and called for the resignation of Gyanesh Kumar, head of the Election Commission of India (ECI), alleging that the revision had improperly removed millions of names from voter lists.
Critics have accused Kumar of acting at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party.
The ECI, the constitutional body responsible for conducting elections in the world's largest democracy, has rejected allegations of wrongdoing.
On Monday, a three-judge bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant issued notices to the government, the ECI and Kumar after hearing petitions challenging decisions linked to the voter list revision.
Another hearing is expected to be held next week.
One of the petitions sought a probe into ECI records to determine whether its decisions complied with constitutional requirements.
Protests have been held across several cities since a report last month by The Indian Express, which said two of the ECI's three members had formally objected at least 14 times to key decisions linked to the voter roll revision.
"Newspaper reports may be 100 per cent correct, partially correct or incorrect. We cannot pass an order on that basis today. We would definitely want their response. If we find there were instances where law wasn't followed, we can undo it," broadcaster NDTV quoted the bench as saying.
The ECI says the revision exercise, which started last year, is intended to identify fraudulently registered voters and prevent "foreign illegal immigrants" from voting.
Critics say the drive has disproportionately affected marginalised and minority communities, especially Muslims.
India's main opposition Congress party has announced a protest march to the Election Commission's offices in New Delhi on Tuesday, to be followed by nationwide "Save Democracy" rallies.
Among those joining the protests are supporters of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), a satirical political movement that emerged online in May and succeeded in its campaign to oust the then education minister.
The group has called for a "mass mobilisation" in the capital on Saturday.
Police have maintained a heavy presence around the government-designated protest area near New Delhi's Jantar Mantar, and dozens of demonstrators were briefly detained over the weekend.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Genting founder's grandson seeks removal of late mother's RM1.6b estate administrators
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The interim administrators of late Genting heiress Lim Siew Kim's RM1.6 billion estate allegedly paid lawyers over RM2 million without approval, breaching a court order, the High Court heard today.
The administrators, lawyer Datuk S. Satharuban and Khoo Siew Kiat were appointed by the High Court on Nov 27, 2023, to manage the estate administrators pendente lite amid an ongoing family dispute over the validity of Siew Kim's will.
Siew Kim, the third child of late Genting Group of Companies founder Tan Sri Lim Goh Tong, died of cancer in July 2022 at the age of 73.
She left behind three daughters and an only son, Marcus Chan Jau Chwen, 42, who is seeking the removal of the administrators.
Lawyer Datuk Kamarul Hisham Kamaruddin, representing Marcus said the disputed payments included RM1.4 million and more than RM800,000 paid to lawyers in 2024.
He said the payments were allegedly made despite an earlier court order requiring payments relating to debts other than those of Siew Kim to be subjected to the court's scrutiny.
"The court order is absolutely binding and commands obedience. It is because those orders are breached that this removal application has been brought before the court," he said during submissions.
Kamarul Hisham argued that scrutiny required the court to consider and approve the payments before they were made, rather than merely receiving a report from the administrators afterwards.
"The court cannot be reduced to a passive recipient of information after the fact.
"Scrutiny must mean the court looks at it before the payment is made," he said.
He said the scrutiny had to be exercised by the court itself, as the administrators were under the court's control and direction.
Kamarul Hisham said Satharuban and Khoo, as officers of the court, were required to act impartially and comply with its orders and directions.
He also submitted that the threshold for removing the administrators was whether there was a reasonable suspicion of misconduct or whether they were unsuitable to continue in the role.
Among Marcus' complaints are allegations that payments were made from individual accounts instead of the designated trust account, that estate funds were depleted through improper payments, and that the administrators interfered in companies linked to the estate.
He further alleged that the administrators nearly caused the estate to pay RM4.73 million in assessments on behalf of Prominview Sdn Bhd, despite the liability allegedly resting with a joint-venture partner.
Other complaints include the administrators' alleged lodging of private caveats and undertaking of property valuations despite having no authority to distribute or dispose of estate assets.
Marcus also alleged that Satharuban and Khoo had treated him with suspicion from the outset, which he said undermined their duty to remain neutral.
In the second will dated April 11, 2022, Siew Kim reduced the cash bequests for her second and third daughters, Chan T'shiao Li,48, and Kimberly Chan Tshiao Miin,45, to RM900,000 and RM100,000 respectively, prompting the siblings to contest their late mother's will involving assets valued at more than RM1.6 billion.
Marcus was granted 30 per cent of the residuary estate along with authority over all her safe deposit boxes.
Siew Kim's eldest daughter, Cressa Chan T'shiao Yunn, was left RM10 million and property in Ampang Hilir, Kuala Lumpur. Cressa's daughter, would receive RM50,000 a month.
Satharuban and Khoo took over the administration of the estate after T'shiao Li and Kimberly filed a probate suit on Jan 19, 2023, challenging a will said to have been executed on April 28, 2022.
On Jan 23, Marcus obtained an ad interim injunction restraining Satharuban and Khoo from acting for the estate pending disposal of the removal application.
The first and second defendants named in the suit filed by the sisters are Malcolm Fernandez and Chan Mei Yee – the executors and trustees – named in Siew Kim's will dated April 28, 2022.
The third and fourth defendants are Marcus and lawyer Datuk Low Beng Choo, who had drafted, prepared and executed Siew Kim's third will on April 28, 2022.
T'shiao Li and Kimberly are challenging the validity of the will, arguing that their mother lacked testamentary capacity due to her medical condition prior to death.
Marcus was also represented by lawyers Goik Kenwayne and Foong Kar Yee.
Lawyer B. Thangaraj acted for Satharuban and Khoo.
The hearing before High Court judge Datuk Mahazan Abdul Taib continues on Wednesday.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar: Malaysia must move beyond traditional manufacturing, strengthen AI capabilities
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia must move beyond traditional manufacturing and strengthen its capabilities in high-end technology, particularly artificial intelligence.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said this is important as the country seeks to navigate an increasingly competitive global economic landscape.
In a Facebook post, he said he held discussions with prominent figures from the technology and academic sectors at the Khazanah Megatrends Forum 2026, where technological transformation, geopolitics and Malaysia's economic future were discussed.
He said discussions with semiconductor industry leader Datuk Fong Swee Kiang centred on the need for Malaysia to strengthen its capabilities in high-end technology and benefit from the ongoing AI-driven technological transformation.
"We were on the same page about the need for Malaysia to move beyond traditional manufacturing and strengthen our capabilities in high-end technology, particularly the AI super-cycle," he said.
Anwar also held discussions with Professor Charles O'Reilly and Professor Stephen Kotkin on transformative change and the need for institutions to move up the technological value chain.
He said the discussions also covered the evolving geopolitical and economic landscape, including rivalry among major powers and its implications for Malaysia.
He added that technological advancement and economic progress must be accompanied by good governance and strong institutions.
"There can be no compromise in our fight against corruption and abuse of power," he said.
He said Malaysia's ability to benefit from technological transformation would depend not only on its capacity to develop high-end industries, but also on the strength and integrity of its institutions.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Defence Ministry seeks more funding in 2027 Budget
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Defence Ministry hopes the 2027 Budget, to be tabled on Friday, will provide sufficient funding to strengthen the readiness of the armed forces.
He said the allocation should take into account the country's needs, particularly to ensure that the armed forces had sufficient capabilities to defend the country and safeguard its sovereignty.
"I believe the Prime Minister will give due consideration based on the country's needs and our need to defend the country and safeguard its sovereignty.
"We also need to take into account the challenges we face and the current geopolitical situation," he said at the Siber Siaga 2026 press conference.
On Aug 7, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government would continue efforts to
increase defence allocations
through the 2027 Budget to strengthen the armed forces' readiness and ensure the welfare of security personnel.
He said defence allocations had increased by more than 35 per cent over the past three years, adding that further allocations would cover areas including servicemen's housing, the construction of new hospitals and maintenance of basic facilities such as water supply.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said the increase was possible amid an improving economic outlook, supported by a stronger ringgit, higher foreign investment and controlled inflation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man charged with murder of Indian domestic helper
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A businessman was charged at the magistrate's court here today with murdering his domestic helper last month.
Stevent Anthony, 31, was accused of murdering Tamilarasi Kumar, an Indian citizen, at a house in Titiwangsa between 4am and 10.55am on Sept 24.
He was brought before magistrate Khairunissak Hassni after being held under a nine-day remand order.
The accused nodded to indicate that he understood the charge, which was read out in court.
The charge, framed under Section 302 of the Penal Code, carries the death penalty or a jail term of between 30 and 40 years, and not fewer than 12 strokes of the rotan, upon conviction.
No plea was recorded as murder cases fall under the jurisdiction of the High Court.
Deputy public prosecutor Nur Ainna Maryam Nor Azman prosecuted while the accused was represented by lawyers Carenjit Kaur and Khairunissa Azzahrah Ghazalie.
The magistrate denied bail and fixed Dec 16 for the submission of the post-mortem report.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: IJM appoints former KPMG Malaysia managing partner Johan Idris as chairman
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:IJM Corp Bhd has appointed Datuk Johan Idris as its independent non-executive director and chairman of the board, effective today.
The appointment follows the retirement of Tan Sri Datuk Krishnan Tan at IJM's 42nd annual general meeting on Aug 27.
Commenting on his appointment, Johan said he is honoured to join the IJM board and take on the role of chairman.
"IJM has strong businesses, an experienced management team and a clear strategic direction.
"I look forward to working with my fellow board members and management to uphold strong governance and oversight as the company executes its priorities and creates long-term value for its stakeholders," said Johan.
Datuk Lee Teck Yuen, who assumed the chairmanship following Krishnan's retirement, has been redesignated as a non-independent non-executive director.
"I welcome Johan to the IJM board and as chairman. I look forward to working closely with him and my fellow board members while continuing to serve IJM as a non-executive director," Lee said in a statement.
According to IJM, Johan brings over 34 years of experience in finance, audit and strategic advisory.
He was managing partner and country senior partner of KPMG Malaysia from 2014 to 2024, having previously served as its head of audit and an audit partner.
Johan was also president of the Malaysian Institute of Accountants from 2013 to 2015 and an executive member of Bank Negara Malaysia's Financial Stability Executive Committee from 2016 to 2018.
He currently serves as chairman of Maxis Bhd and non-executive chairman of KPMG Malaysia, as well as a director of KLCC Property Holdings Bhd and KLCC Real Estate Investment Trust.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: AG's Report: Six 12MP projects face delays, contract terminations
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Six development projects under the 12th Malaysia Plan faced implementation issues, including contract terminations, prolonged extensions of time (EOT) and delays.
According to the Auditor General's Report 2/2026, the six projects comprised two Armed Forces Family Housing (RKAT) projects, the Galeria Perdana upgrading project in Langkawi, a People's Housing Programme (PPR) project and two fire station quarters projects in Sabah.
The first one, the RM100 million Joint Task Force 2 (ATB 2) RKAT project at Kukusan Camp, Tawau, Sabah, originally scheduled for completion in July 2024, achieved only 28 per cent physical progress as of Dec 31, 2024.
Its contract was terminated on May 23, 2025.
According to the report, the defence ministry project was granted two EOTs totalling 418 days before termination due to the contractor's poor financial management and failure to carry out the works diligently, resulting in site activities coming to a halt.
As of July 30, the Public Works Department (JKR) had prepared tender documents for the appointment of a completion contractor, while an additional RM3.90 million for the project was approved by the economy ministry on Aug 6.
Meanwhile, a RM63.25 million Air Force Base Quarters project in Labuan was granted four EOTs totalling 467 days up to 2025, followed by two additional EOTs totalling 410 days in 2026, with the completion date extended to Nov 17.
The report stated that as of July 30, physical progress stood at only 51 per cent against the scheduled 54 per cent, with delays attributed to factors including a shortage of skilled workers and the need to source raw materials from outside Labuan.
For the RM20.40 million Galeria Perdana Upgrading Project in Langkawi, the contract was terminated on Sept 23, 2024, after four EOTs totalling 192 days had been granted, with Liquidated and Ascertained Damages (LAD) amounting to RM440,000 imposed for a 136-day delay.
The audit found that the project was handed over to JKR in January 2025 for further action, while the estimated cost of completing the project increased by RM36 million to RM56.40 million.
The tender process for appointing a completion contractor is expected to be held in February 2027.
Meanwhile, all 67 units under the RM23.70 million PPR project in Kampung Selagon, Beaufort, which was completed in 2017, remained unoccupied as of July 2026 due to structural damage caused by ground movement.
Thirteen units suffered severe damage, while a RM2.72 million contract for the demolition and reconstruction of eight units and repairs to five others was mutually terminated on March 11, 2025, after physical progress reached only 15 per cent.
The RM14.39 million Semporna Fire and Rescue Station quarters reconstruction project was also terminated on March 11, 2025, after being granted five EOTs totalling 1,164 days.
At the time of termination, physical progress stood at only 25 per cent, with RM2.83 million already spent.
According to the report, the project was terminated due to the contractor's financial incapacity, failure to carry out the works according to schedule, and weaknesses in project management and monitoring.
A retender was advertised in June 2026, and the project is currently at the tender evaluation stage.
Separately, the RM6.85 million Merotai Fire Station and quarters construction project was terminated on Nov 5, 2025, despite having achieved 96.6 per cent physical progress, after seven EOTs totalling 1,075 days had been granted.
In light of the findings, the auditor general recommended that the relevant ministries and departments take immediate action to ensure the projects are completed, enabling the development objectives to be achieved and the targeted groups to benefit from the projects.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Irene's grandfather urges action against those responsible for her death
Article:
BATU PAHAT: The grandfather of 16-year-old Irene Sofiya Mohd Kharool Faisal expressed deep grief today over the death of his granddaughter, who was found dead in a school hall in Yong Peng.
Khyar Abas, 69, struggled to hide his heartbreak over the tragic loss of his granddaughter, affectionately known as Fiya.
"Why did they do this to my granddaughter? What did she do wrong? Even if I cry, Fiya will not return. I only regret that Fiya had to be the victim.
"I leave it to the authorities to conduct a full investigation. Give a fitting punishment to those responsible. We want action taken not just for the family or me, but as a lesson so it does not happen to anyone else," he said after receiving a visit from Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi at his home in Kampung Parit Selamat, Yong Peng, today.
Khyar added that Fiya would usually go to school as normal and greet him, a routine he deeply missed.
"This morning after Subuh prayers, I felt as if Fiya was still here. My heart was heavy, and I cried because I imagined Fiya walking into the room to greet me.
"I miss her, especially when it is time to go to school. Only this morning did I fully realise Fiya is gone, and I must be strong to face this ordeal," he said.
Meanwhile, Onn Hafiz said the state government is prepared to assist with basic requirements, including installing closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras to ensure student safety in schools.
He said student safety in schools must be given serious attention to prevent a recurrence of the tragedy that befell the Form Four student.
"We are aware of what we can assist with at the state government level, and we will help. However, there are thousands of schools in Johor and tens of thousands nationwide under the Education Ministry.
"That is why I feel this matter needs to be examined more closely by the ministry. I will get in touch with them," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MPs seek answers on Flying Doctor Service safety after Sarawak crash
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Two members of parliament have raised concerns over the safety and continuity of the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) following last month's helicopter crash that killed five people in Long Lellang, Sarawak.
Dr Kelvin Yii (PH-Bandar Kuching) questioned the use of a 35-year-old Bo 105 helicopter for the service, as well as the maintenance oversight of aircraft operated by Layang-Layang Aerospace.
He said the helicopter was manufactured in 1991, while production of the model ceased in 2001. He added that the company suspended its entire Bo 105 fleet two days after the crash.
"If the suspension was necessary, why was it not carried out before this tragedy happened?" he said during the debate on the Health Select Committee's report in the Dewan Rakyat.
Yii questioned when the FDS contract with Layang-Layang was awarded, its value and whether it was awarded through an open tender.
He also asked whether the contract stipulated an age limit for aircraft used in the service, and when the Health Ministry last independently audited the company's maintenance records.
Dr Halimah Ali (PN-Kapar) said the committee's recommendation to strengthen mobile outreach services through sufficient manpower, vehicles and equipment must be taken seriously.
She said this was particularly important as the victims had been carrying out their duties and providing healthcare services to communities in remote areas.
Halimah urged the ministry to conduct a comprehensive risk assessment of FDS operations following the tragedy.
She also questioned whether the number of aircraft and other aviation assets currently available was sufficient to serve remote communities relying on the service.
"What is the Health Ministry's plan to ensure continuity of FDS, including replacement aircraft, medical evacuation readiness, training for crews and healthcare workers, and emergency coordination without compromising safety?" she asked.
The
five killed in the crash
were Layang-Layang Aerospace pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30, from Seremban, Negri Sembilan; Health Ministry doctor Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, 33, from Kota Baru, Kelantan; nurses Debra Moset, 40, and Jessie Paya Jok, 44; and medical assistant Alexson Adit Henry, 31.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PN says suspension could shut coalition out of Melaka polls
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Perikatan Nasional (PN) has warned that it could be shut out of the coming Melaka state election if the suspension imposed by the Registrar of Societies (RoS) is not lifted before nomination day.
The coalition said in court papers that the suspension prevents it from carrying out normal political activities, including authorising candidates to contest under the PN banner and using its registered name and symbol.
PN said any court decision in its favour after nomination day could come too late as the opportunity to field candidates under the coalition's banner could no longer be restored.
The matter was raised in a certificate of urgency filed together with PN's judicial review application challenging two notices issued by RoS.
PN said that unless the suspension was stayed or quashed before nomination day, no authorised officer would be able to sign the documents required for candidates to contest under the coalition's name and symbol.
It said the Election Commission was due to meet this Wednesday to fix the dates for the writ, nomination and polling for the 16th Melaka state election.
The coalition said the consequences of the suspension would not only affect the applicants in the judicial review but also its component parties, members and voters in Melaka.
PN is seeking an interim stay of the suspension pending the disposal of its judicial review application.
It is also asking for the substantive judicial review to be heard on an expedited basis in view of the impending state election.
The judicial review was filed by PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan, Wong Chia Zhen of Gerakan, N. Sathes Kumar of MIPP, Datuk Seri Saifuddin Abdullah of Wawasan and Datuk Sazmi Miah of Pejuang.
They named RoS and Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail as respondents.
PN is challenging a notice dated Sept 22 issued under Section 13(2) of the Societies Act and a separate order dated Sept 23 under Section 13(2A) suspending the coalition's activities.
The Sept 22 notice requires PN to show cause why its registration should not be cancelled, while the Sept 23 order bars the coalition from carrying out activities other than those necessary to respond to the notice.
The application is currently at the leave stage.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Good governance key to curbing illegal land encroachment, says Anwar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Good governance and strong enforcement are needed to curb illegal land encroachment, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today.
Anwar stressed that such violations should not be taken lightly as they could affect national planning and public interest.
Speaking after chairing the 83rd National Land Council meeting, Anwar said issues raised by stakeholders, including non-governmental organisations, must be addressed promptly to ensure accurate and transparent communication.
"Good governance must continue to be upheld and any form of illegal land encroachment must not be taken lightly as it could affect national planning and the interests of the people," he said in a Facebook post.
He noted that land management could no longer focus solely on economic gains or physical development, particularly as the country faces the effects of climate change.
"As we face the effects of climate change, land governance can no longer focus solely on economic gains or physical development.
"Land management must be carried out prudently and in a planned manner to minimise risks to environmental sustainability," he said.
Anwar added that the government will continue to ensure that all land management initiatives are implemented responsibly for the benefit of the people.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MPs urge Home Ministry to take over refugee registration
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Government and opposition members of Parliament have urged that the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) no longer be given the mandate to register refugees in the country.
Lawmaker RSN Rayer (PH-Jelutong) said the Home Ministry should be given full responsibility for refugee registration, alongside an integrated nationwide operation to monitor their whereabouts.
"The Home Ministry should be given the full mandate and that an integrated operation be conducted nationwide to
monitor the whereabouts of these refugees,
whose number has reached 220,000," he told the Dewan Rakyat today.
He was speaking during a debate on the briefing on refugee management.
Rayer said Malaysians had been tolerant and compassionate, and willing to help those fleeing difficulties in their home countries.
"However, in recent years, we have seen what happened in the
Wang Kelian tragedy,
where refugees were brought into the country through illegal routes, sometimes becoming victims of human trafficking, being killed and buried along the border," he said.
Meanwhile, Datuk Dr Radzi Jidin (PN-Putrajaya) proposed that the government stop accepting new refugee registrations and that anyone currently in the country without a valid permit be considered an illegal immigrant.
He also called for a review of UNHCR's role in Malaysia, questioning the extent of its authority in determining who qualifies for refugee registration.
"What guarantee is there that refugee registrations carried out by UNHCR are transparent?
"What guarantee is there that syndicates are not registering illegal immigrants as refugees?
"Who gave UNHCR such extensive authority that some refugees believe they are free to do anything with a UNHCR refugee card?
"How long will UNHCR be given the authority to determine who qualifies as a refugee? If UNHCR is given such freedom, this country could face an influx of refugees," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zara inquest: Coroner conducts second site visit to teen's school
Article:
PAPAR: The Coroner's Court today conducted a second site visit to SMKA Tun Datu Mustapha as part of an inquest into the death of 13-year-old Zara Qairina Mahathir.
The visit, from 10am to 1.30pm, was attended by the coroner, deputy public prosecutors, and legal representatives of interested parties.
Several adult witnesses, including teachers, and child witnesses attended the visit to clarify locations, layout, and physical conditions mentioned in earlier testimony.
However, children involved in a proceeding related to Zara Qairina were excluded.
Among the areas inspected were classrooms, the Design and Technology room, hostel dormitories, and hostel toilets. The court conducted its first visit on Sept 11 last year.
A statement issued by the legal team for Noraidah Lamat, Zara's mother, said the visit helped the court and all parties better understand the physical layout referred to in court.
The court has asked parties to consider whether any matters arising from the visit require further clarification or additional evidence to be formally recorded. If necessary, parties may apply to recall previous witnesses.
The inquest resumes tomorrow with testimony from Zara's stepsister, Malianah Mahathir.
The period from tomorrow to Oct 23 has been set aside for remaining witnesses, including Noraidah and investigating officer Inspector Wong Yew Zhung, to take the stand.
Zara Qairina was found unconscious on the ground floor of SMKA Tun Datu Mustapha on July 16 last year and was pronounced dead the following day at Queen Elizabeth Hospital here.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: TA Securities to underwrite SKA Capital's Malaysian public portion in ACE Market IPO
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: SKA Capital Bhd has signed an underwriting agreement with TA Securities Holdings Bhd for its proposed listing on the ACE Market of Bursa Malaysia, where the stock broking company will underwrite the entire portion of the new shares offered to the Malaysian public investors and eligible persons.
The initial public offering (IPO)  involves a public issue of 168.08 million new shares and an offer for sale of 72.4 million existing shares.
Of the new shares, 44.78 million will be offered to Malaysian public investors, while 8.96 million will be allocated to eligible directors, employees and persons who have contributed to the company. This is the portion that TA Securities will be underwriting.
Another 111.94 million shares will be placed with Bumiputera investors approved by the Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry, while 2.41 million shares will be placed with selected investors.
SKA Capital, through its subsidiaries SKA Rekabina and Reltency Engineering, provides power infrastructure engineering services, including substation engineering, engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning, civil and structural engineering, electrical and mechanical engineering, and underground utilities engineering.
It also trades electrical devices, equipment and construction materials.
The company has about 17 years of operating experience and holds a Construction Industry Development Board (CIDB) Grade G7 contractor registration.
It is also registered with Tenaga Nasional Bhd as a supplier and service contractor, the Ministry of Finance for government procurement and the Energy Commission as a Class A electrical contractor.
Managing director Datuk Subas Kumar AL Ambairam said the proposed listing would strengthen the company's financial position and internal capabilities, allowing it to pursue larger projects and broaden its solutions.
He said growth opportunities were supported by rising electricity demand, grid expansion and modernisation, renewable energy integration and the development of data centres and other power-intensive industries.
"We intend to leverage our established track record and resources to pursue larger-scale projects, expand our presence in underground utilities engineering and participate in new projects across Peninsular Malaysia," he said.
TA Securities is the principal adviser, sponsor, underwriter and placement agent for the IPO.
TA Securities head of corporate finance Ku Mun Fong said SKA Capital's TNB vendor registration, CIDB G7 credentials and project experience positioned it to benefit from Malaysia's efforts to develop more resilient power infrastructure.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: IGP: Don’t hide school safety issues to protect reputations
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — Safety issues in schools should not be concealed to protect reputations, as this may prevent authorities from taking action, said Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail.
He said cooperation between the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) and schools should be strengthened to ensure all incidents are reported for further action.
“Sometimes there are actions by certain parties attempting to hide issues to protect their reputation. But I believe if we enhance and strengthen this relationship, it can help resolve the problems,” he told a press conference after the launch of the PDRM Negotiator Handbook at the Bukit Aman Senior Officers' Mess here today.
Mohd Khalid said school safety is a shared responsibility requiring cooperation among PDRM, schools, the Ministry of Education, and parents. School liaison officers also regularly visit and coordinate with school authorities on safety issues.
He added that PDRM holds regular discussions with schools and parent-teacher associations on safety measures, including proposals to install closed-circuit television (CCTV). The Crime Prevention and Community Safety Department (JPJKK) has also increased patrols at schools and hostels.
On the death of a 16-year-old student at a school in Yong Peng, Johor, he said some details remain unconfirmed and the department will conduct a thorough investigation before making any conclusions.
Meanwhile, Mohd Khalid said PDRM has strengthened its Negotiator Cell, which was set up two years ago, by introducing a handbook for officers to use during crisis negotiations.
He said the cell, under the Internal Security and Public Order Department (KDNKA), has about 40 officers from various departments. The officers are selected based on their experience and can be deployed if a crisis requires negotiation expertise.
"If a crisis such as a kidnapping occurs, requiring advice, views, or negotiation between relevant parties, we will call upon the officers concerned to carry out the negotiation," he said.
He said the Negotiator Cell also works with other PDRM divisions as needed. The unit has also given lectures and shared experience in crisis management with the Royal Brunei Police Force.
Bukit Aman KDNKA deputy director (Crisis and Disaster) and Negotiator Cell commandant Datuk M.V Srikumar Nair said no standard response time is set for each case, as the duration depends on the circumstances and uniqueness of an incident.
"Every case is unique. Some information is received quickly, while other cases take time. Therefore, there is no standard response time," he said. — Bernama

Title: Johor MB: State government ready to help schools review security measures following student’s death
Article:
BATU PAHAT, Oct 5 — The Johor state government is ready to review and assist with basic infrastructure needs in schools across the state to strengthen security measures, says Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi.
He said this is to prevent a recurrence of the incident that led to the death of 16-year-old Form Four student Irene Sofiya Mohd Khairool Faisal at a secondary school in Yong Peng, near here.
Onn Hafiz expressed full support for any initiative implemented by the Education Ministry (MOE), particularly the installation of closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras in strategic areas within school premises.
"We have received a report on the incident and will look into every angle and opportunity to ensure student safety is better guaranteed," he said, adding that he would liaise with the ministry regarding student safety issues.
Speaking to reporters after visiting the victim's family in Kampung Parit Selamat today, he expressed deep sorrow on behalf of the state government, while urging the public to give police space to conduct a thorough investigation and refrain from speculation.
Meanwhile, State Education and Information Committee chairman Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali said discussions would be held soon between the Johor State Education Department (JPNJ) and the Batu Pahat District Education Office (PPD).
He said the meeting would re-examine safety standard operating procedures (SOPs) in detail to address any existing weaknesses or shortcomings.
"This is not a matter to be taken lightly as it involves the loss of a life," he said.
On Saturday (Oct 3), Irene Sofiya was found unconscious and bleeding in the school hall at about 5.50 pm.
Johor Police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said the victim sustained injuries to her head and body and was pronounced dead at the scene.
Police subsequently detained a 16-year-old boy in Yong Peng at about 7 pm the same day. He was later remanded in custody for six days until Oct 9 to assist in investigations under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder. — Bernama

Title: PM Anwar: Land encroachment must be taken seriously
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — Good governance practices must continue to be upheld, while any form of unauthorised land encroachment must not be taken lightly as it could affect national planning and the interests of the people, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
He said enforcement must therefore continue to be strengthened, while any related issues raised by stakeholders, including non-governmental organisations (NGOs), should be addressed promptly to ensure accurate and transparent information is communicated comprehensively and effectively.
In a Facebook post today, Anwar said he stressed these points while chairing the 83rd National Land Council meeting.
“As we confront the effects of climate change, land governance can no longer focus solely on economic returns or physical development.
“Land management must be carried out prudently and systematically to minimise risks to environmental sustainability,” he said.
Anwar said the Madani Government would continue to ensure that land management initiatives were carried out responsibly for the benefit of the people. — Bernama

Title: Warehouse worker pleads not guilty to driving under the influence, injuring two marathon runners
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 —An e-commerce platform warehouse worker pleaded not guilty in the Magistrate’s Court here today to two charges of riding a motorcycle under the influence of alcohol, causing injuries to two participants of a running event last Saturday.
Muhammad Saiful Sabinee, 21, was charged with riding a motorcycle against the flow of traffic with an alcohol level of 184 milligrams (mg) per 100 millilitres (ml) of blood, resulting in injuries to Mazni Lamin, 50, and Azwan Ibrahim, 41, on Jalan Munshi, near a clothing store here, at 6.14 am on Oct 3.
The charges were framed under Section 44(1A)(b) of the Road Transport Act 1987, which provides for a minimum prison sentence of seven years and a maximum of 10 years, as well as a fine of up to RM50,000, upon conviction.
The provision also stipulates that a person convicted may be disqualified from holding or obtaining a driving licence for a period of not less than seven years from the date of conviction.
Earlier, Deputy Public Prosecutor Nurbatrisyia Mohd Razib proposed bail of RM10,000 with one surety for each charge, noting that the accused did not possess a driving licence.
Lawyer Muhammad Iqbal Azmi from the National Legal Aid Foundation, representing Muhammad Saiful, appealed for a bail reduction, saying that his client was single and earned RM1,500 a month.
“My client has four siblings, one of whom is still in school, and his mother is present today to act as his surety,” he said.
Magistrate Aliaa Anwar granted Muhammad Saiful bail of RM500 with one surety for each charge and set Jan 7, 2027, for case mention and submission of documents. — Bernama

Title: Govt launches framework to prepare communications, multimedia workforce for AI-driven changes
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — The federal government today launched a new framework to align communications and multimedia industry needs with education and skills development as artificial intelligence (AI), digitalisation, emerging technologies and the green economy reshape the sector.
Led by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), the Communications and Multimedia Future Skills Framework (C&M FSF) will serve as a strategic reference for talent development in the communications and multimedia sector over the next five to 10 years.
Its implementation will also involve the Higher Education and Human Resources ministries to align industry needs with education and skills development.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the framework identifies industry needs while aligning government, industry and education efforts to keep talent development in step with technological and economic changes.
