“AI is already changing the nature of many jobs, particularly in areas such as advertising, graphic design and production, by speeding up work processes and taking over some tasks.
“So it is a guideline that we will study and apply across specific sectors under MCMC’s purview, particularly broadcasting, telecommunications and postal and courier services,” he told reporters after the launch of the framework at Angkasapuri here.
Fahmi said the framework was not regulatory in nature, but focused on workforce needs and the potential impact of AI adoption on the sectors and their long-term planning.
To ensure the C&M FSF meets industry needs, the Future Skills Talent Council (FSTC) has been established under the Human Resources Ministry in collaboration with the Communications Ministry through MCMC.
Meanwhile, the Higher Education Ministry will use the C&M FSF to strengthen curricula, micro-credentials and graduate competencies, while training and upskilling programmes will be tailored to changing technology and job market needs.
Fahmi said the framework’s launch reflected the federal government’s efforts to anticipate changes in the job landscape and prepare Malaysians with future-ready skills.
“On the government’s part, we will work to ensure there are more job opportunities available, enabling companies to hire more people, especially young Malaysians,” he said.

Title: ‘Touch ‘n Go rep’ scam leaves Kedah woman RM150 poorer, says consumer group
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Oct 5 — A 39-year-old self-employed woman lost about RM150, including her BUDI Madani RON95 (BUDI95) petrol subsidy and reward points, after a phone scammer posing as a Touch ‘n Go representative compromised her e-wallet.
Kedah Consumers Association (Cake) president Mohamad Yusrizal Yusoff said the victim lodged a report at the association’s office yesterday.
“The victim said the caller offered her a new Touch ‘n Go card with various perks, including reward points, store vouchers offering discounts of up to 80 per cent, and overseas spending capabilities.
“After she agreed to apply for the card, the caller instructed her to open her Touch ‘n Go e-wallet application and follow specific instructions,” he said in a statement today.
He added that without her knowledge, the fraudster took over the application and accessed her account.
“Cake has advised her to report the matter to both the police and Touch ‘n Go.
“Several other individuals have since come forward stating they were also targeted. Cake advises the public to exercise caution regarding unsolicited telephone offers, as fraudsters are resorting to various tricks to deceive people,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Penang stays on alert for human rabies after Kedah man dies of infection
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Oct 5 — Penang has recorded no human rabies cases since the last two cases were reported in 1975, with the Penang State Health Department remaining on standby to respond to any possible cases.
State Youth, Sports and Health Committee chairman Daniel Gooi Zi Sen said no animal rabies cases had also been detected in the state to date.
“No new cases have been reported thus far, but we are always prepared to deal with any incidents,” he said at a press conference for the Penang state-level Clean, Smoke-Free Premises Programme at Food Bayana Medan here today.
Gooi said the state government was also working with the Department of Veterinary Services to monitor the rabies situation in Penang.
He advised the public to follow Ministry of Health guidelines if bitten by an animal, including seeking immediate medical attention at any healthcare facility to ensure those exposed to infection risks receive proper examination and appropriate treatment.
On Sept 27, a 31-year-old man from Kubang Pasu, Kedah, died of rabies after reportedly being bitten by a stray dog in August, marking the first human rabies case reported in the state since 1998. — Bernama

Title: High Court rejects Bar bid to challenge Ahmad  Terrirudin’s JAC appointment
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — The High Court today dismissed the Malaysian Bar’s application for leave to commence judicial review proceedings challenging the appointment of Federal Court judge Ahmad Terrirudin Salleh to the Judicial Appointments Commission (JAC), according to a report by
Free Malaysia Today
(FMT).
Justice Norliza Othman, in delivering her decision, held that Section 5(1)(e) of the JAC Act 2009 was unambiguous.
“Section 5(1)(e) is plain. It specifies the category of person: a Federal Court judge; and the appointing authority: the prime minister, and stops there,” she was quoted as saying.
Since both conditions were met, Norliza said the court could not read non-statutory criteria such as seniority, length of service and freedom from unresolved allegations into the provision, as none of those requirements appeared in the legislation.
The court also rejected the Bar’s arguments on illegality and irrationality, saying unproven allegations and inferences could not form the basis of judicial review.
Norliza emphasised that the court’s role was to interpret the law as enacted by Parliament, FMT reported.
Terrirudin, a former attorney-general, was elevated to the Federal Court in November 2024.
The Bar, which represents about 24,000 lawyers in Peninsular Malaysia, filed the application in February, seeking 11 orders, including a certiorari order to quash Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim’s decision to appoint Terrirudin to the JAC on Nov 15 last year.
According to the report, Terrirudin is to serve as a JAC member for a two-year term, from the date of his appointment until Nov 14, 2027.
The Bar also sought a mandamus order compelling the prime minister to exercise his prerogative to appoint a member to the JAC in accordance with the law, established conventions and the JAC Act 2009.
It further sought an order compelling Terrirudin to show cause and disclose the basis of his appointment to the JAC.
The Bar named Terrirudin, Anwar and the government as the first to third respondents.
Lawyers Zainur Zakaria, Ambiga Sreenevasan and Steven Thiru represented the Bar, while senior federal counsels Shamsul Bolhassan and Nurhafizza Azizan appeared for the attorney-general.

Title: PAS MP calls for humane approach to Rohingya refugees amid calls for tighter controls
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — PAS lawmaker Ahmad Tarmizi Sulaiman today called on the government to strike a balance in managing Rohingya refugees, saying a strict immigration policy must also be humane.
“We must protect national security, control our borders, and maintain strong registration systems, but in doing so, we cannot lose our humanity and sense of justice,” Sik MP Ahmad Tarmizi Sulaiman said when addressing the House during a debate on refugee management.
Focusing on the conflict in neighbouring Myanmar as the primary driver of displacement into Malaysia, Ahmad Tarmizi urged Asean to step up diplomatic pressure for a political resolution.
“Refugee flows will not end as long as the causes driving people from their homes remain unresolved,” he said, calling for an end to violence against civilians, particularly in Rakhine State, unhindered delivery of humanitarian aid and inclusive political dialogue.
To address operational issues, Ahmad Tarmizi endorsed government plans for a standardised digital identification system equipped with biometric tracking, background security checks, transparent status determination and inter-agency audit checks.
Such a system, he said, would properly distinguish genuine refugees from economic migrants, undocumented immigrants and victims of human trafficking.
“Refugees are not necessarily illegal immigrants, and victims of human trafficking must not be treated as criminals,” he said, warning against rising hate speech and xenophobia on social media while stressing that human rights protections do not grant non-citizens immunity from local laws.
Ahmad Tarmizi also voiced opposition to any potential government move to invite Myanmar’s military junta leader to diplomatic talks, citing an International Criminal Court (ICC) arrest warrant application against the junta chief.
“Inviting the junta chief would violate our principles and inflict severe diplomatic damage on Malaysia’s global standing,” he said.
Xenophobia, hate speech must stop
The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) said 214,079 refugees and asylum seekers were registered in Malaysia as of December 2025, alongside more than 90,000 individuals detained in enforcement operations in 2025.
Ahmad Tarmizi said the Rohingya community in Malaysia had faced intense xenophobic attacks in recent months, which he attributed to what he described as the government’s failure to manage the refugee issue effectively and counter hateful propaganda.
“Do not allow hate speech and xenophobia to dominate society. While I also want to place very critical emphasis on this issue of refugee management, specifically regarding extreme hatred, hate speech and xenophobia, which are increasingly easy for certain quarters to exploit, particularly through social media,” he said.
“However, I emphasise that upholding humanitarian principles does not mean defending every action of individual refugees,” he added.
“If a refugee commits a crime, breaks the law, disturbs public order, engages in violence, exploits others, or commits any offense, they must face Malaysian law.”

Title: Malaysia’s statutory debt at RM1.295t, or 63.9pc of GDP, still within legal limit, says Auditor General’s report
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — The Federal Government’s statutory debt-to-gross domestic product (GDP) ratio stood at 63.9 per cent last year, remaining below the statutory debt limit of 65 per cent, according to the Auditor General’s Report (LKAN) 2/2026.
According to the report, the statutory debt stood at RM1.295 trillion, comprising Malaysian Government Securities, Malaysian Government Investment Issues and Malaysian Islamic Treasury Bills.
“The statutory debt-to-GDP ratio has shown an upward trend since 2023, rising from 62 per cent to 63.9 per cent.
“This ratio remains below the statutory debt limit of 65 per cent, as stipulated under the Loans (Local) (Statutory Limit on Borrowing) and Government Funding (Statutory Limit on Moneys Received) Order 2022,” it said. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: LKAN stands for Laporan Ketua Audit Negara (Auditor General’s Report).

Title: Woman, 69, found dead in parked car after discharge from Melaka Hospital
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 5 — A 69-year-old woman was found dead in the front passenger seat of a Proton Saga parked at Taman Tasik Utama, Ayer Keroh, here yesterday.
Melaka Tengah district police chief ACP Halim Abas said in a statement today that the woman was found at about 4pm after she was discharged from Melaka Hospital, still wearing hospital clothes with her left arm in a sling.
“The victim was receiving treatment for a fractured left shoulder sustained in a fall at home. Her 44-year-old son received a call from Melaka Hospital at 1.50pm to take her home. She was wearing hospital clothes as she had no spare clothes,” he said.
Halim said the woman arrived at the car park at about 2.50pm but reportedly refused to get out of the car, adding that at 3.30pm, her 47-year-old neighbour found her unconscious, with one leg outside the vehicle.
He said the woman had a history of diabetes and had previously received treatment at Melaka Hospital, with an examination of her body finding no suspicious injuries and no criminal elements detected.
Halim said the case has been classified as sudden death, with a post-mortem examination scheduled at the Forensic Medicine Department of Melaka Hospital today. — Bernama

Title: Electric buses hit the test track as Rapid Penang gears up for greener rides
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Oct 5 — Rapid Penang will conduct test runs of two electric buses on Oct 6 and 7, marking an initial step towards the introduction of electric buses into Penang’s public transport system.
In a statement today, Rapid Penang said the initiative was part of Rapid Bus Sdn Bhd’s ongoing efforts to replace existing buses with safer, more sustainable and environmentally friendly vehicles, while enhancing operational efficiency.
“The test run involves two electric buses from different manufacturers, namely a 12-metre Foton bus and an 8.25-metre Golden Dragon bus.
“Both buses will undergo separate test runs on selected routes to assess their suitability and operational capabilities under real-world conditions, including energy consumption, charging performance, passenger safety and comfort,” the statement said.
Rapid Penang said preparations would also be made to support electric bus operations, including the provision of charging infrastructure, maintenance facilities, staff training and other operational support requirements.
The statement said electric buses would be introduced in stages after the test runs, as Rapid Penang continued to enhance its operational readiness and make improvements to ensure smooth service delivery for passengers.
Meanwhile, Rapid Bus Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Syahrul Azmir Ahmad Zaki said the test run formed part of Rapid Penang’s efforts to introduce electric buses in Penang, in line with its phased bus replacement programme.
“This provides a crucial benchmark to ensure our operations team has sufficient data and experience to assess the performance, capabilities and operational requirements of electric buses under real-world conditions before they are introduced on existing routes,” he said.
Rapid Penang is currently in the first phase of procuring 75 electric buses, with deliveries scheduled in stages through March 2027.
The procurement is part of Penang’s ongoing phased bus replacement programme, involving 240 electric buses and 70 new diesel buses. — Bernama

Title: Chicken curry, evening drives and a white cat: Song Swee Guan’s family remembers the man behind the Sarawak politician
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 5 — Sarawakian statesman Datuk Song Swee Guan has been remembered as a selfless and caring man who was able to balance between work and family.
Grieving family members remember the former assemblyman, MP, State Legislative Assembly (DUN) Speaker, and Kuching South’s first mayor as someone who quietly sacrificed so much for others.
According to Song’s niece Kaylene Tan, his dedication to his work and selfless care for his parents kept him single.
“I believe he was a very good son. My grandfather – his father – was bedridden for many years and he would look after him, especially when he was unwell at night. When he needed attention at night, my uncle would go there and help him and look after him.
“I was still very little at that time, but what was amazing was that he was able to balance his service to the community in Kuching as well as his parents effortlessly. And he never brought the work home,” she told
The Borneo Post
at her uncle’s wake.
Tan said when Song was at home, he was fully focused on the family, his parents, cooking, and having a laugh with them.
Sarawakian statesman Datuk Song Swee Guan was known to be a good cook by family members. — The Borneo Post pic
“Years later, after my grandfather passed away, my uncle continued caring for my grandmother. He made sure she ate well, that she had company, made sure that she was driven from place to place. So, he was a very good son,” she said.
Reflecting on her uncle’s lesser-known qualities, she revealed that he loved to cook, noting that he cooked delicious chicken curry and kacang ma.
She said Song used to bring her sister, brother, grandmother, and herself for long evening drives around Kuching city.
“He was like a hero. Whenever he stopped at the shops or the wet markets, he said: ‘I don’t want to go out,’ from the car because he would be ‘flooded’ by all these hawkers.
“And that was during his time as the mayor. He was very popular with the people,” she recalled.
Song Chai Kim (left) and her daughter Kaylene Tan (right) share their memories of her brother and Tan’s uncle, the late Datuk Song Swee Guan, at home. — The Borneo Post pic
She also shared that Song loved cats and theorised on the inspiration behind the famous white cat statue in Padungan.
“You know that white cat statue? At the time when it was launched back then, my grandmother had a white cat.
“I’m not so sure if the white cat statue was inspired by the white cat,” Tan said.
Tan’s mother Song Chai Kim remembered how close she and her older brother were.
“Oh, we had a very happy childhood together, played together, did a lot of things together. We were very close.
“He went overseas to study at a very young age, then I got married and I’ve been staying in Singapore since then.
“Despite the distance, we still managed to maintain a close relationship. We were a very close family,” she said.
Song’s foster son Sim Min Min said they often spent time together over coffee.
“We were close. He was like a father figure to me, and he considered me as a son.
“He was a well-mannered man who loved to help people and he would try to help them however he could,” Sim said.
Sim Min Min recalls time spent over coffee with Sarawakian statesman Datuk Song Swee Guan, whom he described as ‘a father figure’. — The Borneo Post pic
He added for the past 20 years, Song had been an active hiker until he suffered mobility issues.
Song was appointed a councillor of the Kuching Municipal Council (KMC) in 1981 before becoming its chairman in 1982.
He led the council until 1988 and subsequently became the founding mayor of Kuching South in August that year, following the delineation and establishment of Kuching South.
Song served for four terms as Padungan assemblyman from 1983 to 2001 and as Bandar Kuching MP from 1995 to 2003.
He was also DUN Speaker from 1996 to 2000.
He passed away peacefully on Sunday at 3.30pm at Sarawak General Hospital. — The Borneo Post
* Editor’s note: DUN is an abbreviation in Malay for Dewan Undangan Negeri, or the State Legislative Assembly.

Title: Planes, not just ships: Myanmar says most migrants returned from Malaysia flew home, as UN criticises Putrajaya’s scheme
Article:
YANGON, Oct 5 — Myanmar has repatriated nearly 10,000 migrants from Malaysia this year, state media said on Monday, a day after a flotilla returning almost 1,500 of its citizens docked in the country.
The United Nations (UN) has sharply criticised Malaysia’s push to return migrants to Myanmar under an opaque scheme it says cannot guarantee safe homecomings to the war-torn nation.
A group of 1,476 returnees arrived by ship outside Yangon on Sunday, the first of 5,000 that Kuala Lumpur says Myanmar agreed to take back amid a wave of anti-migrant sentiment in Malaysia.
Rights monitors have raised concerns that members of the Rohingya minority may be sent back to Myanmar, where they have faced violent persecution, but Malaysia has not commented on the ethnicities of returnees.
Myanmar revealed on Monday that a parallel and larger repatriation push has also been taking place by plane.
Between January and August this year, “8,041 citizens were repatriated by air”, state newspaper
The Global New Light of Myanmar
said.
While the ship returns have been highly publicised in Malaysia, Kuala Lumpur has not commented on the returns Myanmar says it organised by weekly flights.
The total number of migrants Myanmar has said returned by plane and ship this year is 9,517.
Malaysia insists returnees under its scheme agreed to voluntary repatriation from detention centres, where Myanmar says they had “faced difficulties” after serving sentences for immigration offences.
But rights groups report dire conditions in the facilities, and the UN refugee agency says staff were not allowed to verify that decisions to return were “were genuinely free and informed”.
More than 100,000 people are estimated to have been killed in Myanmar since a military coup in 2021 unleashed civil war, according to monitor organisation ACLED.
The Rohingya started fleeing the country en masse to Malaysia before that, escaping a military crackdown starting in 2017 deemed a genocide by rights groups — a charge the armed forces have always denied.
The Rohingya make up two-thirds of the 190,000 Myanmar refugees and asylum seekers in Malaysia, according to UN data, and have been the focus of recent anti-migrant sentiment.
After the ships carrying the 1,476 migrants docked Sunday in Thanlyin, just south of Yangon, AFP journalists saw dozens moved to a monastery holding centre for ID and health checks.
“Necessary arrangements are continuing to facilitate their swift reunion with relatives and family members, ensuring their safe return to their respective hometowns,”
The Global New Light of Myanmar
said. — AFP

Title: Police vow no cover-up in probe into schoolgirl’s death in Yong Peng
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — Police have pledged a thorough and transparent investigation into the death of a 16-year-old girl who was believed to have been murdered at a school here on October 3.
Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk M. Kumar said the investigation would be conducted comprehensively and professionally, with no attempt to cover up the case or protect any party.
“The investigation will be conducted comprehensively, transparently and professionally without any element of cover-up or protecting any party,” he said in a statement.
The case is being investigated by the Batu Pahat district police headquarters’ Criminal Investigation Division under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder.
A 16-year-old boy was arrested on October 3 and has been remanded for six days from October 4 to 9 to assist investigations.
A post-mortem conducted at Hospital Sultanah Nora Ismail in Batu Pahat on October 4 found the cause of death to be blunt trauma to the head.
Police said the school and Education Ministry were cooperating fully with the investigation.
They also advised the public against speculation or comments that could interfere with the investigation or manipulate facts in a way that could cause public concern.
The case remains under investigation.

Title: Yong Peng school had CCTV but none at the crime scene, security firm under probe, says Fadhlina
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — The secondary school in Yong Peng, Johor, where a Form Four female student was allegedly found murdered, is equipped with CCTV cameras, but none were installed at the location where the incident occurred.
Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said the Ministry of Education (MOE) is now upgrading the CCTV facilities and has launched an investigation into the school’s security company to determine whether there were any breaches of standard operating procedures (SOPs).
“The school does have CCTV, but the cameras were not installed at the scene of the crime. That is why I say, beyond the (new installation) phases...
“...any school that already has CCTV, but where the system is non-functional or damaged, should inform us so that we can work together to improve its functionality, ensuring it can capture and record events within the school,” she told a press conference at the Parliament building today.
Elaborating on security measures, Fadhlina said the ministry is also conducting a comprehensive review of the patrol records and duties carried out by the security company on the day of the incident.
She warned that financial penalties or termination of the contract could be imposed if any breaches of the stipulated terms are found.
Meanwhile, she urged the public to stop spreading false information about the incident out of respect for the grieving family of the victim and the underage suspect, who remains under police investigation.
“There have been claims that the victim was dragged from the surau (prayer room) to the hall where the incident occurred, as well as allegations of broken glass in the surau. None of this is true.
“Let us not add to the pain with speculation,” she said.
While extending her condolences to the victim’s family, Fadhlina said the ministry demanded that justice be served in the death of Irene Sofiya Mohd Khairool Faisal, 16, and had fully entrusted the criminal investigation to the Royal Malaysia Police .
“Regarding Irene Sofiya, our responsibility now is clear. The truth must be uncovered, and justice must be served. Justice for Irene Sofiya,” she said.
Irene Sofiya was found dead, with injuries on her body suggesting that she had been murdered, inside the hall of a secondary school in Yong Peng at 5.30pm last Saturday.
The victim was discovered by her grandmother and a friend, who had gone to the school after realising that she had not returned home even though her extra classes had ended. — Bernama

Title: Record RM4.64b income, highest payout in eight years: Zulkifli Hasan says Tabung Haji’s governance now stronger
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — Lembaga Tabung Haji’s (TH) new and existing investments have shown positive results following the transformation and strengthening of governance processes, said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan.
This development is reflected, among other things, in TH recording its highest investment income in history, he said.
“We have recorded the highest profit in the history of TH since last year. This demonstrates the success of new and existing investments.
“The transformation carried out has also further strengthened governance,” he said during Dewan Rakyat’s oral question-and-answer session today.
He was responding to Datuk Che Mohamad Zulkifly Jusoh (PN-Besut), who asked the Prime Minister to outline the government’s strategy for diversifying TH’s new investment portfolio and strengthening its risk management framework to ensure the sustainability of the institution’s funds.
Zulkifli said TH has a systematic investment process, which includes assessing investment, risk and shariah aspects before making any investment decision.
“TH has implemented a prudent, shariah-compliant investment strategy guided by the strategic asset allocation (SAA) framework to ensure that its investment portfolio has an appropriate level of diversification across asset classes, sectors and markets.
“The SAA is reviewed every three years to ensure that TH’s investment strategy and risk management take into account current factors affecting the changing dynamics of the economic environment and capital markets,” he said.
For the 2025 financial year, TH’s investment income rose to RM4.64 billion, the highest level recorded. Total assets were RM98.58 billion versus liabilities of RM95.63 billion.
The profit distribution rate also increased progressively from 1.25 per cent in 2018 to 3.50 per cent in 2025, the highest in eight years. — Bernama

Title: No mandatory e-Consular registration yet, but foreign minister wants Malaysians abroad to sign up to make contact in emergencies easier
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — The government does not yet intend to make registration on the e-Consular system mandatory for Malaysians abroad, said Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan.
He said registration through the digital platform managed by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs remains voluntary, but Malaysians residing, travelling or studying abroad are highly encouraged to register to facilitate monitoring and welfare matters.
“Not yet (making registration mandatory). We have not yet considered applying to the government to make it mandatory, but we hope that tourists and Malaysians abroad will use this facility.
“This e-Consular application makes it easier for embassies and diplomatic missions to know the whereabouts of our citizens, while also allowing us to contact them in case of any crisis, natural disaster or emergency,” he said during the question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He was replying to a supplementary question from Khairil Nizam Khirudin (PN-Jerantut), who wanted to know whether the government plans to make registration on the e-Consular system mandatory.
Earlier, Datuk Seri Sh Mohmed Puzi Sh Ali (BN-Pekan) asked about the government’s measures to tighten the registration system for Malaysians travelling or residing abroad to ensure they can be detected and assisted promptly in the event of a tragedy, disaster or emergency.
Commenting on the MyWorldAlert safety application, which is now integrated with e-Consular, Mohamad said it functions as a rapid communication system based on the Global Positioning System (GPS), capable of delivering important information and alerts immediately during urgent situations.
Meanwhile, in response to a supplementary question from Sh Mohmed Puzi regarding assistance in bringing back citizens stranded abroad, he said the ministry provides consular assistance in terms of family communication and facilitating the process of savings or fundraising.
“We provide various forms of assistance, but we do not fully bear the financial burden. However, cases like pilgrims stranded in Jeddah and Madinah due to being cheated by unauthorised agents who only bought one-way tickets without return tickets, we still help manage (this),” he said.
Commenting on the developments of the flood tragedy in Nepal that occurred on Aug 26, Mohamad said that 54 Malaysians are still categorised as missing or unaccounted for.
“Although the Nepalese government has halted search and rescue (SAR) operations and shifted to the recovery phase, we have not given up and are still in contact with local police to check the registration books at every trekking route post,” he also said.
He added that Wisma Putra, along with various agencies including the Attorney-General’s Chambers, Bank Negara Malaysia and the National Registration Department, is facilitating the affairs of the heirs, especially concerning applications for the release of death certificates with the relevant ministries in Nepal. — Bernama

Title: Prosecution to call up to 20 witnesses as GISBH money laundering trial proceeds at Shah Alam court
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 5 — The Sessions Court here was informed today that the representation submitted by the former chief executive officer (CEO) of GISB Holdings Sdn Bhd (GISBH) and three former company accountants to drop money laundering charges against them had been rejected.
Following this, Deputy Public Prosecutor (DPP) Mohd Ashrof Adrin, who appeared alongside DPP Muhamad Ehsan Nasarudin, said the prosecution would proceed with the trial.
“I regret to inform the court this morning that the prosecution wishes to state that the representation has been rejected and the prosecution will proceed with the trial.
“We will be calling between 15 and 20 prosecution witnesses, and regarding the trial dates, I believe we will require six to eight days,” he said during case management proceedings before Judge Datin Fatimah Zahari.
The four accused are Nasiruddin Mohd Ali, 67, who faces 77 charges involving more than RM10 million; Hamimah Yakub, 74, facing 95 charges involving RM11.4 million; Asmat @ Asmanira Muhammad Ramly, 46, facing 68 charges involving RM4.7 million; and Mohd Khushairi Osman, 55, facing 91 charges involving nearly RM12 million.
However, lawyer Datuk Rosli Kamaruddin, representing all four accused, informed the court that the defence intends to submit a new representation once the seized assets are officially returned to his clients.
He said the new representation would, among other matters, address the possibility of resolving the case through a compound offer.
“For the record, the previous representation did not address the issue of exploring a compound, so there may be a representation exploring this issue,” said Rosli, who was accompanied by lawyer Muhammad Zaim Rosli.
He also requested the court to fix a case management date to determine the status of the new representation in January 2027.
After hearing submissions from both parties, Fatimah fixed the trial for April 26 to 28, June 28 to 30 and July 6 to 8 next year, while the status of the second representation by all four accused will be heard on Jan 26.
Meanwhile, Rosli also sought the court’s permission for the return of Nasiruddin’s passport to enable him to travel to Mecca. Nasiruddin, who appeared in court in a wheelchair, intends to meet his fourth wife, Ummu Mubaroqah Ashaari, 32, who is scheduled to undergo a Caesarean section this month.
He said Muhammad Saleh Basharahil Hospital in Makkah had advised Nasiruddin to be present to provide consent for his wife’s surgery, as she is now full-term, although the exact date of the procedure has yet to be determined.
Mohd Ashrof Adrin informed the court that the prosecution did not object to the application, subject to the conditions stipulated in the notice of application, including that the passport be returned to the court on or before Nov 10, 2026.
The judge subsequently allowed the application subject to the stipulated conditions.
On Sept 10, 2025, Nasiruddin and the three former company accountants pleaded not guilty at the Shah Alam Sessions Court to money laundering charges brought against them.
The alleged offences were committed at bank branches in Selangor between 2020 and 2024 and involved transactions with various parties, including bank accounts belonging to GISBH Sdn Bhd, GISB Mart Sdn Bhd, GISB Travel and Tours Sdn Bhd and childcare centre companies.
They were charged under Section 4(1)(b) of the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 (Act 613), punishable under Section 4(1) of the same Act.
If convicted, an offender is liable to imprisonment for a term not exceeding 15 years and a fine of not less than five times the amount or value of the proceeds of unlawful activity at the time the offence was committed, or RM5 million, whichever is higher. — Bernama

Title: Govt’s dividend income edges up 1.4pc to RM39.55b, with Petronas paying most of it, says A-G
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — The Federal Government received investment dividends amounting to RM39.547 billion in 2025, an increase of RM535 million or 1.4 per cent from RM39.012 billion in 2024.
According to the Auditor General’s Report (LKAN) 2/2026 on the Federal Government Financial Statements for the Year 2025, the dividends were received from 20 companies and two statutory bodies, compared with 21 companies and two statutory bodies in the previous year.
“In 2025, the highest dividend was contributed by Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas), amounting to RM32 billion, while Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) recorded a significant increase in dividend payments, rising by RM2.40 billion,” according to the report released today.
Based on the report, BNM’s dividend increased to RM5.25 billion in 2025 from RM2.85 billion in 2024, while Khazanah Nasional Bhd’s dividend increased to RM2 billion in 2025 from RM1 billion in 2024.
The total dividends of statutory bodies increased by 81.8 per cent to RM5.275 billion from RM2.902 billion, while the total dividends of companies decreased by 5.1 per cent to RM34.271 billion from RM36.109 billion.
“Overall, the dividend receipts from nine companies and one statutory body amounted to RM7.433 billion compared to RM3.982 billion in 2024, an increase of RM3.451 billion (86.7 per cent).
“However, the dividend receipts from 12 companies and one statutory body showed a decline in 2025 compared to 2024, while three companies paid the same amount of dividends in both years,” according to the report.
Regarding investments, the report stated that the Minister of Finance Incorporated (MoF Inc) held investments with a book value of RM34.117 billion in 2025, a decrease of RM131 million or 0.4 per cent from RM34.248 billion in 2024.
“This decline is due to the redemption of Redeemable Cumulative Preference Shares owned by MoF Inc in Syarikat Bekalan Air Selangor, amounting to RM131.00 million, and the full redemption of MoF Inc’s shares amounting to RM1.00 in Hicom Holdings Bhd,” according to the report.
Overall, the Federal Government has stakes in 109 companies, four statutory bodies and one international agency, with the company category recording a value of RM33.103 billion or 97 per cent of the total RM34.117 billion.
The report also stated that the book value of the Federal Government’s investment in Bank Pembangunan Malaysia Bhd increased by RM1.517 billion due to the acquisition of shares by MoF Inc in exchange for its shares in Export-Import Bank of Malaysia Bhd and Small Medium Enterprise Development Bank Malaysia Bhd. — Bernama

Title: Binning edible food a ‘grave sin’, says housing minister as nearly 16,000 tonnes tossed daily
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — Nearly 40 per cent of the 40,000 metric tonnes of solid waste generated in the country daily consists of food waste, according to Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming.
He said efforts to address the waste issue require the cooperation of all parties through a “whole-of-nation approach” involving both businesses and consumers to collectively change their attitudes and practices.
“This is a form of waste. Food waste is not a crime, but it is a sin. It is a grave sin when edible food is simply thrown away,” he said during the question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Nga said this when replying to a question from Datuk Mumtaz Md Nawi (PN-Tumpat) regarding the latest developments in efforts to reduce waste sent to landfills and increase recycling rates.
Meanwhile, he expressed confidence that the ministry would achieve its target of exceeding a 40 per cent recycling rate by the end of this year.
Nga noted that under the “Trash to Cash” recycling programme, the total collection of recyclable materials between January and August exceeded 7.86 million kilogrammes (kg), with a sales value of over RM2.85 million.
“Secondly, the zero-waste community initiative involving the establishment of 17 active zero-waste community centres during the same period has collected over 111,504 kg of recyclable materials,” he said.
Additionally, Nga said a school-based recycling competition involving 1,680 schools successfully collected 4.95 million kilogrammes of recyclable materials, which were sold for RM2.98 million.
“Based on calculations of the total collected from 2018 to last year, we managed to gather nearly 20 million kilogrammes of recyclable items, generating proceeds exceeding RM10.22 million,” he said.
Responding to a supplementary question from Mumtaz regarding the specific controls and enforcement actions implemented by the Ministry of Housing and Local Government concerning cable theft, including penalties imposed on third parties or buyers, he said the Cabinet views the issue seriously.
“We constantly collaborate and engage with the Ministry of Home Affairs, including examining the need to amend relevant laws to ensure harsher penalties are imposed on cable theft offenders in the country.
“There have been several instances where LRT (Light Rail Transit) operations were disrupted due to cable theft by syndicates; therefore, this matter (amending laws for heavier penalties) is crucial to ensuring we continue to safeguard public safety and the well-being of the people,” he said. — Bernama

Title: State audits flag governance weaknesses despite clean financial opinions
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — Six states received an Unmodified Opinion, while another six received an Unmodified Opinion with an “Other Matters” paragraph; one state received an Unmodified Opinion with both an “Emphasis of Matter” paragraph and an “Other Matters” paragraph.
The National Audit Department (JAN), in a statement regarding the Auditor General’s Report (LKAN) 2/2026 today, announced that these findings follow the completion of audits on all 13 State Government Financial Statements for the year ending Dec 31, 2025.
JAN also issued Auditor General’s Certificates for 298 State Agencies for the 2024 financial year and reported the results of performance audits conducted on 22 State Government programmes and activities.
Additionally, the audit of State Government-owned companies reported the results of detailed audits carried out separately on 12 such companies across 11 states: Sabah, Sarawak, Selangor, Johor, Kedah, Pahang, Kelantan, Terengganu, Perak, Melaka and Negeri Sembilan.
According to JAN, significant issues were identified, revealing weaknesses in corporate governance compliance that require the attention of management and the State Governments.
LKAN 2/2026, covering the Federal Government Financial Statements for 2025, activities of Federal Government Ministries/Departments, State Government and State Agency Financial Statements, activities of State Ministries/Departments/Agencies, and the management of State Government-owned companies, was tabled in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Meanwhile, as of September 28, 2026, a total of 12,117 or 94.4 per cent of the 12,835 issues followed up by JAN have been successfully resolved.
JAN said follow-up actions regarding audit issues have contributed to revenue collection and repayments to the government totalling RM920.91 million; this includes funds recovered through penalties, outstanding rent, Liquidated Ascertained Damages (LAD), land lease arrears, as well as the collection of duties and taxes.
According to JAN, all issues raised in LKAN are continuously monitored via the Auditor General’s Dashboard (AGD) online portal until the responsible parties implement resolution measures.
The department noted that the Auditor General has submitted 38 audit recommendations through LKAN 2/2026 for implementation by the audited Federal Ministries and Departments; these recommendations can be accessed on the AGD portal at Auditor General’s Dashboard.
LKAN 2/2026 reports a total of 650 issues within the AGD system, comprising 347 issues still under follow-up, 23 resolved issues and 280 issues requiring no further action (NFA).
“The Auditor General remains independent and firm in providing audit opinions and reporting findings without compromise.
“The LKAN does not merely record shortcomings; it serves as an instrument to drive corrective action, strengthen governance and ensure accountability for every ringgit of public funds in the interest of the people,” the statement read. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: JAN is the abbreviation for Jabatan Audit Negara (National Audit Department), while LKAN stands for Laporan Ketua Audit Negara (Auditor General’s Report).

Title: Targeted subsidy reforms help cut Malaysia’s 2025 bill by RM15.67b, federal audit shows
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — The government has managed to reduce its subsidy expenditure by 40.1 per cent to RM23.43 billion in 2025 from RM39.10 billion in 2024, supported by the decline in crude oil prices and the implementation of the targeted diesel and petrol subsidy reforms.
According to the Auditor General’s Report (LKAN) 2/2026 on the Federal Government’s Financial Statements for 2025, the RM15.67 billion reduction was partly attributable to a significant decrease in petroleum product subsidy, from RM34.91 billion in 2024 to RM19.11 billion in 2025.
“The reduction in subsidy expenditure was partly due to the decline in global crude oil prices and initiatives to reform targeted diesel subsidies from June 2024 and petrol subsidies from September 2025,” the report said.
It said the average global crude oil price fell to US69.05perbarrelin2025fromUS80.81 per barrel in 2024.
Petrol subsidy expenditure fell 46.5 per cent year-on-year (y-o-y) to RM10.51 billion from RM19.66 billion in 2024, while diesel subsidy expenditure declined 48.2 per cent y-o-y to RM5.98 billion from RM11.54 billion previously.
Meanwhile, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) subsidy expenditure decreased 29.1 per cent y-o-y to RM2.63 billion from RM3.71 billion previously.
At the same time, expenditure on welfare grants and assistance for communities, individuals and families increased 380.8 per cent to RM20.36 billion in 2025 from RM4.24 billion in 2024.
“The increase in expenditure was partly due to the disbursement of Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA), Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR), the Madani Subsidy Assistance Programme (BUDI Madani) and STR operating costs,” the report said. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: LKAN stands for Laporan Ketua Audit Negara (Auditor General’s Report).

Title: RM68.81m in contractor advance payments still unrecovered, Audit Dept finds
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — A total of RM68.81 million in contractor advance payments (WPK) involving 24 projects under five ministries remains unrecovered, with 86.7 per cent of the amount outstanding for more than a decade, according to the Auditor-General’s Report (LKAN) 2/2026.
The five ministries involved are the Ministry of Education (KPM), Ministry of Defence (MINDEF), Ministry of Home Affairs (KDN), Ministry of Transport (MOT) and Ministry of Works (KKR).
The audit found that, overall, the management of WPK by the five ministries complied with the prevailing circulars and financial regulations governing eligibility requirements for contractor advance payments.
“However, the outstanding WPK receivables remained a concern, particularly as a significant portion had been outstanding for more than 10 years and involved companies that had either been dissolved or wound up.
“RM59.63 million out of RM68.81 million in WPK receivables outstanding for more than 10 years involved 21 companies,” the report read.
The report stated that five of the companies had been dissolved, involving WPK receivables amounting to RM10.68 million, while 13 companies had been wound up, involving outstanding WPK of RM27.76 million.
Another three companies remained active, with outstanding WPK amounting to RM21.19 million.
The audit noted that the RM10.68 million owed by dissolved companies could not be recovered, while delays in taking follow-up action against companies that had been wound up had also hindered efforts to recover the outstanding amounts.
Among the delayed actions was the submission of the Proof of Debt Form to the Department of Insolvency (MdI), which is necessary to establish the Government’s claim against companies undergoing winding-up proceedings.
Meanwhile, RM9.18 million in WPK receivables had been outstanding for less than five years, involving three companies that remained active.
The audit also uncovered a reporting issue involving RM5.67 million in WPK balances linked to two projects under KPM and MOT.
The amount had not been reported as WPK receivables, resulting in the actual position of outstanding WPK not being accurately reflected.
The audit called on the ministries to take immediate action to strengthen recovery efforts and ensure that the Government’s financial interests are protected.
For companies that had been wound up under KPM and KKR, the ministries were urged to follow up by submitting the Proof of Debt Form to MdI and obtaining the status of dividend distribution to safeguard the Government’s interests.
The audit also recommended that KPM and KDN take immediate action to initiate civil proceedings or issue letters of demand against companies that remain active if there had been a breach of contract.
Such action, it said, was necessary to ensure that statutory provisions relating to limitation periods were complied with and that the prescribed time limits were not exceeded.
For MOT, the audit recommended that WPK receivables be reported immediately once a Termination Notice is issued to a company.
This would ensure that the reported figures accurately reflect the actual outstanding WPK balance that remains to be recovered.
The findings underscore the need for ministries to strengthen monitoring and follow-up action on contractor advance payments, particularly where companies face financial difficulties, winding-up proceedings or termination of contracts, to prevent public funds from remaining outstanding for prolonged periods.

Title: Puspakom opens Kajang centre with capacity to inspect 800 vehicles daily
Article:
KAJANG, Oct 5 — Puspakom Sdn Bhd today began operations at its new inspection centre in Bandar Teknologi Kajang, with the facility eventually able to handle up to 800 vehicles a day.
The centre, which is being opened in stages, will serve motorists and light commercial vehicle operators in Kajang, Semenyih, Beranang, Bangi and surrounding areas.
Private vehicle inspections began today, while Routine and Re-Routine inspections for light commercial vehicles will be introduced on October 28, followed by Initial and Re-Initial inspections from November 23.
Puspakom said the phased opening was aimed at ensuring operational readiness while providing customers with a smoother inspection experience.
The facility has 10 inspection lanes, split equally between private and commercial vehicles, making it the company’s largest centre dedicated to these categories.
It also features an air-conditioned waiting area and a redesigned interior incorporating Puspakom’s corporate identity for the first time at one of its branches.
Puspakom chief executive officer Mahmood Razak Bahman said the new centre was part of the company’s efforts to expand access to inspection services and keep pace with growing demand in southern Selangor.
“The Kajang branch has been designed to provide greater capacity, smoother customer flow and a more efficient inspection experience while maintaining the high standards of vehicle inspection that Malaysians expect from Puspakom,” he said.
The centre will also be used to develop Puspakom’s inspection technology, with AI-assisted checks covering undercarriage and above-carriage inspections scheduled to begin in November.
Mahmood said the initial AI implementation would focus on collecting data and improving the technology’s capabilities.
The opening follows the closure of Puspakom’s Pandan Mewah branch on Sept 30, with customers previously served there able to use the Kajang centre or other nearby branches, subject to available appointment slots.
The Kajang centre is located at Lot 1A & 1B, Jalan P4/13, Bandar Teknologi Kajang, 43500 Semenyih, and operates from 8am to 5.30pm Monday to Friday.
Appointments can be made through GiCheck.

Title: Perikatan parties file judicial review challenging ROS suspension, show-cause letter
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) leaders have filed a judicial review challenging the Registrar of Societies’ (ROS) indefinite suspension of the coalition’s activities, as well as a notice requiring them to explain why the bloc should not be deregistered.
PAS secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said the application for judicial review was filed by the secretary-generals of all PN component parties.
Takiyuddin said the coalition wants the court to quash the show-cause notice under Section 13(2) of the Societies Act 1966 and a subsequent order suspending all its activities indefinitely.
“The only reason given (for the two directives) was only that we did not invite Bersatu leaders for a meeting on July 16, 2026.
“But the official complaint by Bersatu was never communicated to us,” the PAS leader and Kota Bharu MP told reporters here today.
The meeting was called to discuss electoral preparations and other coalition matters, he added, noting that PN decided not to invite Bersatu following a July 15 decision by Bersatu’s top leadership to bypass the coalition’s shared banner for the polls.
PN, through its lawyers, had on September 24 sought a meeting with the ROS but has yet to receive a response.
Takiyuddin said the coalition wants the judicial review application to be expedited given that the Melaka state election is approaching.
Coalition leaders said the ROS suspension could disrupt PN’s preparations for the Melaka state polls, with it still unclear whether the coalition can contest under its own banner.
The applicants named ROS director-general Datuk Mohd Zulfikar Ahmad and Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail as respondents.
“We request that the ROS make clear the status of whether PN as a registered political coalition can contest in any elections in Malaysia and therefore name any candidates in any elections, particularly at the upcoming Melaka state polls,” Takiyuddin said.
“And also to avoid confusion we would also request for the official explanation of what Bersatu’s complaint content was regarding us,” he added.

Title: ‘Who sent the threats?’ Businessman seeks answers from police a year after Caprice case classified NFA
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — Maritime industry executive Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan, who was investigated over alleged threats made against social media influencer Caprice and his family, wants to know whether anyone has since been identified as being behind the threats.
The chief executive officer of Maritime Network Sdn Bhd said a year had passed since Caprice lodged the complaint against him, and it was important for him to know the outcome, particularly as he had been questioned by police for several hours before the case was classified as no further action (NFA).
“I totally understand that the police investigated based on Caprice’s complaint. I’m not questioning the authorities, but I would like to know the status of the case as I gave my full cooperation to the police.
“The allegation was serious as it tarnished my name and caused embarrassment. I was questioned by police for several hours during the investigation last year, yet no charges were subsequently brought against me.
“I therefore want clarification on what happened to the case and whether anyone has been charged. How many people were called to give statements in connection with the case?” he said in a statement today.
Jeyenderan also called on Caprice and the police to clarify whether the person or persons behind the alleged threatening messages had been identified.
He stressed that he was not seeking to interfere with the authorities’ decision, but wanted a clear explanation of how the case had concluded.
Caprice lodged the police report on July 10 over an Instagram message that allegedly contained a threat. The case was investigated under Section 507 of the Penal Code.
In November last year, the investigation paper was referred to the Selangor Deputy Public Prosecutor’s Office and was subsequently classified as NFA.
In July last year, Caprice also published several Instagram posts, including photos and videos of Jeyenderan, which allegedly linked the businessman to various criminal activities without credible evidence.
Jeyenderan subsequently filed a defamation suit against Caprice, claiming the posts had damaged his reputation and caused him financial losses.
The trial is scheduled to begin at the High Court here in February 2027.

Title: Audit Dept says 12MP development spending exceeds final allocation by RM6.08b
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — Overall expenditure on development projects under the 12th Malaysia Plan (12MP) exceeded the final allocation of RM391.776 billion by RM6.076 billion, according to the National Audit Department.
In a statement on the Auditor-General’s Report 2/2026 released today, the department said an audit of the implementation of development projects under RMK-12 found that total development expenditure amounted to RM397.852 billion.
However, the report said the amount remained within the approved expenditure ceiling.
“Additional allocations were approved for individual projects whose expenditure exceeded their initial allocations,” the report said.
As at December 31, 2025, 3,120 (32.6 per cent) of the 9,578 projects had been completed, while 4,057 (42.4 per cent) remained under implementation.
Meanwhile, 2,208 (23 per cent) projects were at the pre-implementation stage, while 193 (2 per cent) had been cancelled or placed under “keep in view” status.
The audit recommended that the ministries and agencies concerned take proactive measures to strengthen project risk management mechanisms and conduct closer, continuous monitoring to enable early intervention when weaknesses in project implementation are identified.
It also recommended that technical studies and comprehensive assessments of project sites be conducted at the early design stage to prevent changes in scope and increases in project costs.
The audit said these measures were important to ensure projects did not encounter problems during implementation, were completed according to schedule and delivered their intended benefits to target groups.

Title: Drug addict numbers hit 130,307 as of June says home minister
Article:
BENTONG, Oct 5 — A total of 130,307 drug addicts were recorded in the country as of June, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
He saId Terengganu, Kelantan, Kedah, and Perlis recorded worrying trends in drug use and abuse, exceeding the national ratio of 381 cases per 100,000 population.
“For every 100,000 people, Terengganu recorded 735 individuals, while Kelantan recorded 694, Kedah 669, and Perlis 646. Thus, all of them surpassed the national ratio,” he said during a press conference held in conjunction with the handover of the completed project to build, demolish, and upgrade the Karak Narcotics Addiction Rehabilitation Centre (PUSPEN) here today.
Meanwhile, he noted that based on the profiles of the addicts, the 15-to-39 age group constituted the largest segment involved, while in terms of education, the majority held the Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) qualification or lower.
“When looking at employment status, the highest number were unemployed, followed by the self-employed and those working in the private sector. These three employment categories account for a significant percentage of those involved,” he said.
Saifuddin Nasution said amphetamine-type stimulants (ATS) or synthetic drugs are the most widely used substances among addicts, accounting for 84 per cent of drug use.
“These figures are not merely data; they send a distinct signal. That is why I have urged the National Anti-Drug Agency (AADK) to ensure that planned programmes are data-driven and that policies are formulated based on data,” he said.
He added that the Ministry of Home Affairs (KDN) is open to intensifying campaigns and collaborative efforts including with state governments to address this issue.
Furthermore, he noted that tackling the drug problem requires strong political will and cooperation from all parties, as the issue is no longer merely an individual problem but has become a national one.
“Firstly, in terms of politics, there must be strong political will to overcome or combat this scourge. Secondly, we must first agree that the drug problem is no longer just an individual issue; it has become a national problem,” he said.
Also present were Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi, Bentong Member of Parliament Young Syefura Othman, and AADK director-general Datuk Ruslin Jusoh. — Bernama

Title: Health ministry: 3,025 offered places in ILKKM pre-service programme
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, 5 Okt (Bernama) --
Some 3,025 new trainees have been offered places in the pre-service programme at the Ministry of Health Malaysia Training Institutes (ILKKM) for the October 2026 intake.
In a statement today, the Ministry of Health (MOH) said 2,995 of the 3,025 offers were made through the Public Services Commission (SPA), while 30 were for statutory bodies, representing 90.7 per cent of its total quota of 3,335 places.
Of the total places offered, 2,961, or 97.9 per cent, were for 10 diploma-level programmes requiring three years of study, while the remaining 64 places, or 2.1 per cent, were for the two-year Dental Surgery Assistant Certificate programme, it said.
"The Diploma in Nursing programme has the highest intake quota for this session, with 1,818 candidates offered places,” the statement said.
MOH said the intake reflects its continued commitment to developing human capital and producing a competent healthcare workforce over the next two to three years to meet the nation’s healthcare needs.
The statement said trainees would be guided through theoretical learning, practical training and clinical exposure to master professional skills, prioritise patient safety and deliver quality services rooted in empathy.
"Throughout their studies, trainees will also be guided to uphold values such as integrity, discipline, professionalism, teamwork, loyalty to the nation and the principles of public service.
"The development of knowledge, skills and character is crucial to producing a dedicated healthcare workforce that understands its responsibility to safeguard the well-being of the community,” MOH said.
The ministry added that graduates who successfully complete their training could serve in various healthcare disciplines, including nursing, medical and health services, pharmacy, diagnostics, rehabilitation and dentistry.
— Bernama
